result: Participants reduced the benchmark score by 86.1%, with the best circuit using 1,151 qubits and 1,299,453 average Toffoli gates, and a single-call windowed variant using 1,162 qubits and 1,684,161 average Toffoli gates.
conclusion: Open autoresearch can complement human and AI efforts on machine-checkable objectives, though the results do not establish a full-Shor break or formal dominance over prior work.

title: Dependency-Aware Rom/cbd Correctness Bounds For Ml-kem-768 At The Heuristic Failure Scale
authors: Aur\'elie Duriez (nethsys SARL, Lille, France), Christophe Tommasini
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We certify an honest-decapsulation failure upper bound for ML-KEM-768 in an explicit random-function/centered-binomial (ROM/CBD) abstraction. Domain-separated public-matrix streams are modeled as independent uniform ring elements and secret/noise polynomials as independent CBD2 primitives; this is not an information-theoretic statement about the fixed SHAKE instantiation of FIPS 203. Recent formal assessments identify rigorous justification of ML-KEM's heuristic decapsulation-failure scale as an open problem; within the explicit ROM/CBD abstraction studied here, we obtain a dependency-preserving certified upper bound at that scale. The analysis preserves dependencies induced by the public matrix and by both ciphertext-compression terms. Its terminal chain has three components: an exact graph-coupled full-ideal reference for the joint c_u/c_v residual; a proper-ideal bivariate Fourier transport whose rare |T|>=3 branch is closed by an exhaustive three-factor anti-concentration replay; and exact bit-specific FIPS decoding events followed only by a 256-coordinate union bound. A formal partial-Fourier lemma makes the spectral-to-total-variation step explicit. The reduced rational certificate satisfies Pr[K' != K] <= P_* <= 2^-164.81, with -log2(P_*) = 164.810716201343121.... The 164.81 threshold is exact but numerically tight: the certified exponent exceeds it by only about 0.0007162 bit, and 164.82 is not certified. The result is an upper bound for an arbitrary message fixed independently of the public and secret randomness, under honest encryption and decapsulation. It is not an exact DFR, not a fixed-SHAKE equivalence theorem, not a new IND-CCA reduction, and not an adaptive delta-correctness result.
tldr: Certifies an upper bound on the decapsulation failure probability of ML-KEM-768 under an explicit ROM/CBD abstraction.
motivation: The heuristic decapsulation-failure scale of ML-KEM lacks rigorous justification, and recent formal assessments identify this as an open problem.
method: Models public-matrix streams as independent uniform ring elements and secret/noise polynomials as independent CBD2 primitives, then uses a graph-coupled ideal reference, bivariate Fourier transport, anti-concentration replay, and a union bound.
result: The reduced rational certificate gives Pr[K' != K] <= P_* <= 2^-164.81, with -log2(P_*) = 164.810716201343121..., and the bound is numerically tight to about 0.0007162 bit.
conclusion: This is an upper bound for an arbitrary fixed message under honest encryption and decapsulation, but it is not an exact DFR, a fixed-SHAKE equivalence theorem, a new IND-CCA reduction, or an adaptive delta-correctness result.

title: On The Evolution Of The Capacity-Achieving Input Support For The Amplitude-Constrained Awgn Channel
authors: Alex Dytso Luca Barletta
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an additive white Gaussian noise channel subject to a peak-amplitude constraint and study how the support of the capacity-achieving input distribution (CAID) evolves as the amplitude constraint [MATH] varies. Although the CAID is known to be unique, symmetric, discrete, and finitely supported, the structure of its support transitions has remained largely unresolved. We show that the origin is the only possible degenerate support point and the only possible inactive contact point of the KKT function. We then establish continuity properties of the optimal distribution and the KKT function and prove that every nonzero support point is locally stable: under small changes in [MATH], it persists as a unique nearby atom whose location and probability mass vary continuously. Combining these results, we prove that, locally, the support cardinality at a nearby amplitude is either unchanged or larger by one and that any such increase can occur only at the origin. Consequently, all local changes in support cardinality are confined to the origin: locally, the only possible transition mechanisms are the appearance or disappearance of the point at the origin and the splitting or merging of the origin into a symmetric pair.
tldr: The paper characterizes how the support of the capacity-achieving input distribution for the amplitude-constrained AWGN channel evolves as the amplitude constraint varies, showing all local cardinality changes occur only at the origin.
motivation: The CAID for the peak-amplitude-constrained AWGN channel is known to be unique, symmetric, discrete, and finitely supported, but the structure and transitions of its support as a function of the constraint had remained largely unresolved.
method: The authors analyze the KKT conditions of the capacity optimization, prove continuity properties of the optimal distribution and KKT function, and establish local stability of every nonzero support point under small changes in the amplitude constraint.
result: The origin is shown to be the only possible degenerate support point and the only possible inactive contact point of the KKT function; every nonzero support point persists locally as a unique nearby atom with continuously varying position and mass.
conclusion: Locally, the support cardinality either stays the same or increases by exactly one (only at the origin), so the only possible transition mechanisms are the appearance/disappearance of the origin point or its splitting/merging into a symmetric pair.

title: Proximity Gaps For Gabidulin Codes And Applications
authors: Songsong Li, Chaoping Xing, Chen Yuan, Ruiqi Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proximity gaps are central to the soundness of interactive oracle proofs of proximity (IOPPs) and polynomial commitment schemes (PCSs). An [MATH] linear code [MATH] has a [MATH]-proximity gap with error [MATH] if, for every [MATH], either all points on [MATH] are [MATH]-close to [MATH], or at most an [MATH] fraction are. Although proximity gaps for Hamming-metric codes are well understood, their rank-metric counterparts remain largely unexplored despite their applications in coding theory and cryptography. In this work, we study proximity gaps for linear rank-metric codes and their cryptographic applications. First, we show that every [MATH] linear rank-metric code [MATH] over [MATH] admits a proximity gap for every [MATH], with error at most [MATH], where [MATH]. For Gabidulin codes, we improve the gap to [MATH] with error [MATH]. These two proximity gaps match those for general linear Hamming-metric codes and Reed--Solomon (RS) codes, respectively. We prove the [MATH] bound is tight by constructing an infinite family of constant-rate Gabidulin codes and affine lines [MATH] on which a [MATH] fraction of points are [MATH]-close to the code, while [MATH] is at least [MATH]-far from it. At the [MATH] gap, we also give a counterexample establishing a lower bound on [MATH]. As applications, we construct an IOPP for interleaved Gabidulin codes by adapting the Ligero IOPP for interleaved RS codes. We then adapt the Ligero-based PCS for ordinary polynomials to obtain a [MATH]-linearized polynomial commitment scheme. To our knowledge, this is the first PCS framework based on rank-metric error-correcting codes.
tldr: The paper establishes proximity gaps for linear rank-metric codes, with tight bounds for Gabidulin codes, and applies them to build IOPPs and the first rank-metric-based polynomial commitment scheme.
motivation: Proximity gaps underlie the soundness of IOPPs and polynomial commitment schemes, but while the Hamming-metric case is well understood, rank-metric counterparts had been largely unexplored despite applications in coding theory and cryptography.
method: The authors prove that every linear rank-metric code admits a proximity gap for all parameters, improve the gap for Gabidulin codes, and construct tightness counterexamples via constant-rate Gabidulin codes and affine lines; they then adapt the Ligero IOPP/PCS to the rank-metric setting.
result: They obtain proximity gaps matching those of general linear Hamming-metric codes and Reed-Solomon codes respectively, prove the sqrt-bound tight, and construct an IOPP for interleaved Gabidulin codes plus a linearized polynomial commitment scheme.
conclusion: The work opens the study of rank-metric proximity gaps and yields the first PCS framework based on rank-metric error-correcting codes, with relevance mainly to classical coding theory and cryptographic proof systems.

title: Fpga Acceleration Of Fully Homomorphic Encryption With Adaptive Key Switching
authors: Zhihan Xu, Jayashree Adivarahan, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor K. Prasanna
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving cloud services but incurs substantial computation overhead, making hardware acceleration essential. Among FHE operations, key-switching is a major performance bottleneck. Recent cryptographic advances introduce a novel key-switching method (i.e., KLSS) that reduces certain operational complexity but demands higher computational precision than the traditional Hybrid Key Switching (HKS) method. This trade-off leads to distinct computation and memory requirements, making the relative latency of KLSS and HKS highly dependent on hardware parallelism, FHE security parameters, and available on-chip memory capacity, particularly on FPGA platforms, where memory resources and parallelism must be carefully balanced. In this work, we first propose a memory-efficient KLSS datapath that eliminates off-chip ciphertext transfers. We then develop a performance model to analyze and compare the overheads of both KLSS and HKS. Our analysis reveals that an adaptive solution supporting both methods can achieve lower overall latency than a static method during FHE computation. Guided by the performance model, we design an adaptive FPGA-based FHE accelerator that dynamically selects between HKS and KLSS during computation. We implement the accelerator on an Alveo U280 and evaluate it across multiple FHE benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that our adaptive solution achieves a 1.84-3.31[MATH] speedup in bootstrapping latency and a 1.66-2.52[MATH] speedup in secure image classification compared to state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators.
tldr: This paper designs an adaptive FPGA accelerator for Fully Homomorphic Encryption that dynamically switches between two key-switching methods (HKS and KLSS) to minimize bootstrapping latency.
motivation: FHE enables privacy-preserving cloud computation but is bottlenecked by key-switching overhead, and the newer KLSS method trades higher computational precision for lower operational complexity, making the optimal choice hardware-dependent.
method: The authors propose a memory-efficient KLSS datapath eliminating off-chip ciphertext transfers and build a performance model comparing HKS versus KLSS overheads, then use it to design an adaptive FPGA accelerator implemented on an Alveo U280.
result: The adaptive accelerator achieves 1.84-3.31x speedup in bootstrapping latency and 1.66-2.52x speedup in secure image classification compared to state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators.
conclusion: Dynamically selecting between HKS and KLSS based on hardware parallelism, security parameters, and memory capacity yields substantially lower FHE latency than any static approach.

title: Perfect Combinatorial Structures In Coding Theory And Cryptography
authors: Vladimir N. Potapov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This book develops algebraic and combinatorial methods for studying discrete structures. It brings together graph theory, Boolean functions, Fourier analysis on finite groups, coding theory, perfect colorings and perfect codes, association schemes, Latin squares, and related topics. A central theme is the interaction between different representations of the same object: combinatorial, algebraic, spectral, and coding-theoretic. The main mathematical object studied in this book is a perfect coloring of a graph, or, equivalently, an equitable partition of a graph. The book is intended for advanced undergraduate and graduate students in mathematics and computer science, as well as for researchers in discrete mathematics, combinatorics, coding theory, and related fields.
tldr: A mathematics textbook that develops algebraic and combinatorial methods for classical discrete structures such as perfect colorings of graphs, perfect codes, Boolean functions, and Latin squares.
motivation: The book aims to unify diverse representations (combinatorial, algebraic, spectral, coding-theoretic) of the same discrete object to support study and teaching in discrete mathematics and combinatorics.
method: It synthesizes graph theory, Fourier analysis on finite groups, association schemes, coding theory, and perfect colorings/perfect codes, centering on equitable partitions of graphs as the main object of study.
result: The outcome is an expository volume presenting interconnections among classical combinatorial, algebraic, and coding-theoretic frameworks rather than new quantum information results.
conclusion: The work is a classical discrete-mathematics reference with no quantum information, quantum entropy, cryptography-security-proof, or thermodynamic content, making it only tangentially related to the listed research directions.

title: Arithmetic Scar Accessibility And Generic Schrodinger Control On Metric Graphs
authors: Binh T. Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study internal exact controllability of the free Schr\"odinger equation on finite compact metric graphs with Kirchhoff conditions at interior vertices and a fixed Dirichlet-Neumann assignment at exterior vertices. For a prescribed primitive cycle or exterior-to-exterior path, we identify an arithmetic criterion ensuring that the corresponding scar is accessible by exact high-frequency eigenfunctions of a fixed target metric. The criterion is formulated by intersecting the regular scar stratum of the secular set with the orbit-closure torus of the target length vector, and it can hold for resonant metrics beyond the rationally independent class. Under an intrinsic Diophantine condition on the orbit-closure flow, the construction is quantitative: along an exact eigensequence the mass outside the prescribed support decays polynomially, yielding a polynomial degeneration law for finite-frequency observation when that support is uncontrolled. Rationally independent metrics have full phase-orbit closure and therefore make every primitive obstruction accessible. Combining this spectral result with the known graph-theoretic characterization and sufficiency of the Graph Geometric Control Condition (GGCC), we prove that, for every rationally independent and hence for Lebesgue-almost every metric, GGCC is necessary and sufficient for exact controllability at every positive time in the free setting.
tldr: The paper establishes arithmetic conditions for scar accessibility and proves that the Graph Geometric Control Condition is necessary and sufficient for exact controllability of the free Schrödinger equation on metric graphs for rationally independent metrics.
motivation: Exact controllability of the Schrödinger equation on metric graphs is a fundamental control-theoretic problem, and the role of eigenfunction scars and arithmetic properties of graph lengths in this context is not fully understood.
method: The authors intersect the regular scar stratum of the secular set with the orbit-closure torus of the target length vector, impose an intrinsic Diophantine condition on the orbit-closure flow, and combine the resulting spectral analysis with the known Graph Geometric Control Condition (GGCC).
result: For rationally independent metrics, every primitive obstruction is accessible, and along an exact eigensequence the mass outside the prescribed support decays polynomially; consequently, GGCC is necessary and sufficient for exact controllability at every positive time for Lebesgue-almost every metric.
conclusion: The work provides a generic characterization of exact controllability for free Schrödinger equations on metric graphs and quantifies finite-frequency observation through polynomial degeneration, highlighting the role of arithmetic and Diophantine conditions.

title: Reconstructing Fluid Velocity Fields From Sparse Sensors Using A Variational Quantum Algorithm
authors: Nhat-Quang Nguyen, Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Akash, Kourosh Shoele, Yanzhu Chen, Huixuan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstructing fields governed by nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) from sparse measurements is a challenging task because the governing equations are strongly nonlinear and observations are available at only a few locations. Fluid velocity fields are a representative case. In this paper, we propose a variational quantum algorithm that reconstructs the solution over the entire spacetime domain at once. Rather than marching in time, the method encodes the full discrete spacetime solution in a single variational quantum state, so that all time points are optimized jointly. The cost function combines a sparse-measurement mismatch term with a physics-informed PDE violation term, letting data and the governing equation constrain the solution simultaneously. We demonstrate the method on the one-dimensional Burgers and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations using numerical simulations. The results suggest that variational quantum algorithms with a spacetime encoding scheme offer a compact framework for reconstructing nonlinear PDE dynamics.
tldr: The paper proposes a variational quantum algorithm that encodes a full discrete spacetime solution into a single variational quantum state to reconstruct nonlinear fluid velocity fields from sparse sensor measurements.
motivation: Reconstructing fields governed by nonlinear PDEs from sparse measurements is hard because the dynamics are strongly nonlinear and observations are limited to few locations, with fluid velocity fields as a representative case.
method: A single variational quantum state encodes the entire spacetime solution, jointly optimizing all time points with a cost function combining sparse-measurement mismatch and a physics-informed PDE-violation term.
result: Numerical simulations on the 1D Burgers and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equations show the spacetime-encoding variational approach can reconstruct nonlinear PDE dynamics.
conclusion: Variational quantum algorithms with spacetime encoding offer a compact framework for reconstructing nonlinear PDE dynamics, though only numerical proof-of-concept is provided.

title: Multivariate Quantum State Preparation With Optimized Tensor Networks
authors: Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Lukasz Cincio, Annina Z. Lieberherr, Mekena Mcgrew, Thomas R. Bromley
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantics tensor trains are attracting intense interest for quantum-inspired computing and quantum state preparation. These methods, which approximate continuum functions by representing their amplitude encoding as a matrix product state (MPS), are exceedingly powerful for univariate functions but rapidly become challenging when handling multivariate functions, since the linear chain topology leads to a large distance between highly-entangled qubits. We overcome this limitation by introducing SCENT (Spectral Clustering for Entanglement miNimizing Trees). SCENT is a protocol that utilizes efficiently-computable pairwise entanglement metrics to determine a suitable tree tensor network (TTN) structure, which can then be efficiently approximated using tensor cross-interpolation (TCI); we find that it substantially outperforms MPS methods and improves upon previous TTN methods. We then apply these optimized TTNs to state preparation, introducing an approximate circuit compilation method based on environment-tensor methods without significantly conceding overall accuracy. Importantly, the inherent gauge freedom of TTNs can be directly exploited in this method, resulting in higher fidelity at a given circuit depth. We demonstrate this quantum state-preparation pipeline on archetypal state-preparation problems in quantum chemistry and financial portfolio optimization. In our flagship demonstration, we encode a 20-variable probability distribution with long-ranged, non-nearest neighbor inter-variable correlations in a 200-qubit state-preparation circuit with infidelity [MATH] using only 43284 CNOTs; depth and fidelity can be traded, allowing the same distribution to be prepared to infidelity [MATH] with as few as 5584 CNOTs.
tldr: Introduces SCENT, a protocol that uses pairwise entanglement metrics to design tree tensor network structures for efficient multivariate quantum state preparation, outperforming MPS methods.
motivation: Multivariate function amplitude encoding with quantics tensor trains is challenging because the linear MPS topology creates large distances between highly entangled qubits, limiting efficiency.
method: SCENT selects a tree tensor network structure via efficiently computable pairwise entanglement metrics, then approximates it with tensor cross-interpolation; an environment-tensor-based circuit compilation method exploits TTN gauge freedom.
result: Applied to quantum chemistry and financial portfolio optimization, it encoded a 20-variable probability distribution in a 200-qubit circuit with infidelity [MATH] using only 43284 CNOTs, or infidelity [MATH] with as few as 5584 CNOTs.
conclusion: Optimized TTNs enable practical multivariate quantum state preparation

title: Finite Cores Exhaustion And The Failure Of Strict Sequential-Pressure Approximation In Coded Shifts
authors: C. Evans Hedges
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a coded shift whose generating set uniquely represents its concatenation set. We prove that, for every continuous potential [MATH], the pressures of the finite-generator subshifts (the finite cores) converge to the sequential pressure [MATH], the supremum of free energy over invariant measures giving full mass to the concatenation set. Thus full sequential pressure is the exact condition for the finite cores to recover global pressure. The proof is a refinement of the inducing argument of Burr, Das, Wolf, and Yang. Given an arbitrary enumeration of the generators and a length-ordered enumeration of the language, we obtain an algorithm which computes the global pressure of every computable potential with full sequential pressure. The set of equilibrium states is recursively compact, and a unique equilibrium state is computable from the same data. For the zero potential, [MATH] therefore implies computability of topological entropy and of any unique measure of maximal entropy. We also construct a uniquely represented presentation of the full binary shift for which the zero potential has full sequential pressure but is not a uniform limit of potentials satisfying [MATH], disproving a conjecture of Burr, Das, Wolf, and Yang.
tldr: The paper proves that finite-core pressures converge to the sequential pressure in coded shifts and establishes computability of pressure and equilibrium states under full sequential pressure, while disproving a related conjecture.
motivation: To determine when finite approximations of coded shifts recover global pressure and whether thermodynamic quantities like topological pressure and equilibrium states are computable from finite data.
method: Refines the inducing argument of Burr, Das, Wolf, and Yang, using arbitrary enumerations of generators and length-ordered language to construct an algorithm computing global pressure for computable potentials with full sequential pressure.
result: Finite-core pressures converge to sequential pressure; a unique equilibrium state is computable; the set of equilibrium states is recursively compact; and a counterexample to the Burr–Das–Wolf–Yang conjecture is given.
conclusion: Full sequential pressure is exactly the condition for finite cores to recover global pressure, enabling computability of entropy and equilibrium states, but strict sequential-pressure approximation fails in general.

title: Sharp Conditioning For Matrix Recovery By Finite Affine Orbits
authors: Dongwei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(q=p^h\) be an odd prime power, and let the affine group \(\mathbb F_q\rtimes\mathbb F_q^\times\) act through its canonical \((q-1)\)-dimensional irreducible representation. Qualitative matrix recovery for these rank-one orbits is known. We determine sharp lower singular-value bounds for explicit real generating windows. First, we compute the exact least singular value for every nonnegative two-level window over \(\mathbb F_{p^h}\) with \(h\geq2\), and identify the unique optimizer when \(q-1\geq10\). The resulting conditioning stays bounded away from zero on every fixed odd-characteristic tower and is within an explicit characteristic-dependent factor of the best possible value over all real windows. For every \(q=3^h\), \(h\geq2\), we construct a real three-level absolute-trace window (constant on the fibers of \(_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_3}\)) whose least singular value is \[ {q(2-\sqrt2)-1}>\frac1{\sqrt2}. \] For the full class of real windows constant on the three trace classes, we reduce the least singular value to four scalar expressions and a symmetric \(2\times2\) matrix. This yields the exact global optimum and all equality cases: the displayed trace window is uniquely optimal up to global sign and interchange of the two nonzero trace classes. Thus zero trace mean follows from optimality. The proof combines an explicit sum-of-squares identity, uniform quadratic-form certificates, and a finite-geometric block decomposition of the orbit measurement operator.
tldr: The paper establishes sharp lower bounds on the least singular value for matrix recovery using finite affine orbits over odd characteristic fields, with explicit optimal real generating windows.
motivation: Matrix recovery for rank-one orbits under the affine group is qualitatively known, but quantitative conditioning bounds for real generating windows were lacking.
method: The proof uses an explicit sum-of-squares identity, uniform quadratic-form certificates, and a finite-geometric block decomposition of the orbit measurement operator.
result: For every q=3^h (h≥2), a three-level absolute-trace window achieves least singular value q(2−√2)−1 > 1/√2, and the full class of trace-class windows yields exact global optimum and equality cases.
conclusion: The work provides sharp conditioning guarantees for affine-orbit matrix recovery and identifies uniquely optimal windows, showing that zero trace mean follows from optimality.

title: Enhancing Pauli Correlation Encoding For Quantum Optimization Via Systematic Expressivity Analysis
authors: Riku Usuki, Don Arai, Ken N. Okada, Keisuke Fujii
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum approaches for combinatorial optimization problems have attracted considerable attention in recent years. Among these approaches, Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) has emerged as a promising framework for quantum devices with limited qubit resources because it embeds optimization variables in expectation values of Pauli strings. However, the mechanisms underlying its performance and the reasons for its saturation remain unclear. In this work, we investigate these questions through a systematic analysis of expressivity and trainability. First, we compare PCE with classical surrogate models based on tensor networks whose structures progressively approach the topology of the PCE circuit. The results show that PCE attains comparable solution quality with substantially fewer trainable parameters, indicating strong parameter efficiency. Second, to determine whether the performance saturation of conventional PCE is caused by insufficient expressivity or by optimization difficulty, we perform a diagnostic expressivity test in which the circuit is trained toward reference configurations for Max-Cut. The results show that even shallow PCE circuits can represent strong solutions, indicating that the main bottleneck is not the representational power of the ansatz, but the trainability under the relaxed objective function. Motivated by this finding, we propose a multistage continuation framework that gradually transforms a smooth relaxed objective into a sharper objective that more closely approximates the target discrete problem. Numerical experiments on G-set instances with 800 vertices show that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional PCE and is competitive with representative graph neural network (GNN) methods. These results clarify the main factors behind PCE performance and provide a practical strategy for improving PCE on quantum devices with limited qubit resources.
tldr: The paper analyzes Pauli Correlation Encoding for quantum combinatorial optimization and proposes a multistage continuation framework to improve trainability.
motivation: Paul Correlation Encoding is promising for quantum devices with limited qubit resources, but its performance saturation and underlying mechanisms were unclear.
method: The authors compare PCE with tensor-network surrogate models, perform diagnostic expressivity tests on Max-Cut, and introduce a multistage continuation framework that gradually sharpens a relaxed objective.
result: PCE is parameter-efficient, and its bottleneck is trainability rather than expressivity; the proposed method outperforms conventional PCE on 800-vertex G-set instances and is competitive with GNN methods.
conclusion: The work clarifies the factors behind PCE performance and offers a practical strategy for improving quantum optimization on resource-limited devices.

title: Weyl Defects In Skein Theory And Quantum Cluster Charts
authors: Jennifer Brown, Juan Ram\'on G\'omez Garc\'ia, David Jordan, Matthias Vancraeynest
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a modified invertibility property for the parabolic defects introduced in arXiv:2102.12283, arXiv:2505.14836. Namely, we show that the Borel defect cancels its dual, up to insertion of an invertible Weyl defect and up to restriction to an open-subcategory. The main result holds for an arbitrary reductive group [MATH] -- for illustration we give extended computations for [MATH]. Along the way, we introduce a defect skein theory with defects in both codimension one and two, which is compatible with gluing of defect 3-manifolds and defect surfaces. Our results provide a potential defect skein theoretic construction of certain standard charts which appears frequently in quantum cluster varieties associated to surfaces.
tldr: The paper proves a modified invertibility property for parabolic defects in skein theory and relates it to quantum cluster charts.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of defects in skein theory and their connection to quantum cluster varieties associated to surfaces.
method: They introduce a defect skein theory with codimension-one and codimension-two defects, compatible with gluing, and prove that the Borel defect cancels its dual up to an invertible Weyl defect and open-subcategory restriction.
result: The main theorem holds for an arbitrary reductive group, with extended computations for a specific example, providing a potential defect skein-theoretic construction of standard charts in quantum cluster varieties.
conclusion: This work advances the mathematical theory of defects and skein theory, with potential applications to quantum cluster charts, but lies outside the core quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Schur Tests And Estimates For Positive Semigroups On Non Commutative $L_p$
authors: Cl\'ement Coine, M\'elina Laforge, \'eric Ricard
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the recent results of Arnold on estimates for Kreiss positive semigroups on [MATH]-spaces to the non commutative setting, [MATH]. We also provide a sharp example. All the results are achieved thanks to the use of the Schur test, including a new version for von Neumann algebras.
tldr: The paper extends Schur-test-based estimates for Kreiss positive semigroups from commutative Lp spaces to noncommutative Lp spaces over von Neumann algebras.
motivation: Arnold recently obtained estimates for Kreiss positive semigroups on Lp spaces, and the authors aim to generalize these results to the noncommutative setting.
method: The authors develop a new version of the Schur test for von Neumann algebras and apply it to derive estimates for positive semigroups on noncommutative Lp spaces.
result: They establish extended estimates for Kreiss positive semigroups in the noncommutative setting and provide a sharp example showing optimality.
conclusion: The work advances the operator-theoretic understanding of positive semigroups on noncommutative Lp spaces, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Bargmann-Fock Representation And Global Estimates For The Linearized Hard-Sphere Boltzmann Operator
authors: Ilya Karlin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the linearized Boltzmann collision operator for three-dimensional hard spheres and reorganize the complete operator so that its angular and radial structures are explicit before any Sonine truncation. From the Carleman representation, the collision integral becomes a superposition of orthogonal translations; in Hermite/Fock and Bargmann form these generate a single analytic coherent-state kernel for all Hermite collision brackets. Rotational covariance separates fixed angular-momentum sectors, each reducing exactly to a one-variable radial Bargmann space with an [MATH] structure. The radial operator is [MATH], where [MATH] is an explicit Laguerre--Jacobi operator and [MATH] is compact. A unitary intertwiner identifies this realization with the classical Burnett/Sonine coordinate, recovering the Burnett matrix and standard stress and heat-flux corrections. For the untruncated operator, the compact gain gives only compact corrections, while the loss sets the common essential spectrum [MATH]. Radially squeezed [MATH] coherent packets yield threshold Weyl sequences in every fixed angular sector. With [MATH] and squeezing scaled as [MATH], they furnish full-space Weyl sequences throughout the essential band interior, with [MATH], revealing quadratic continuum corridors in the [MATH] plane. At fixed [MATH] and [MATH], the matrix tail approaches a universal Toeplitz operator whose zero at [MATH] is the local signature of the same threshold escape. Thus the Fock reformulation provides exact radialization and constructive control of the global spectral geometry.
tldr: The paper reformulates the linearized hard-sphere Boltzmann collision operator in Bargmann-Fock representation to analyze its radial structure and global spectral geometry.
motivation: Understanding the spectral properties of the linearized Boltzmann operator is important for kinetic theory, but existing Sonine truncations obscure the full operator structure.
method: The author uses Carleman representation, Hermite/Fock and Bargmann coherent-state kernels, and angular-momentum decomposition to separate the operator into radial Laguerre-Jacobi parts plus compact corrections.
result: The full operator's essential spectrum is identified, and radially squeezed coherent packets yield Weyl sequences revealing quadratic continuum corridors in the spectral plane.
conclusion: The Fock reformulation provides exact radialization and constructive control of the global spectral geometry of the linearized hard-sphere Boltzmann operator.

title: Hadamard--Tetrahedral Symmetric Spacetime And Clifford-Like Factorizations Of Dirac And Maxwell Operators
authors: Farhad Aghili
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A symmetric representation of Minkowski spacetime is constructed by combining a normalized fourth-order Hadamard transformation with an imaginary temporal coordinate. The resulting complex coordinates [MATH] distribute time and space equally among four components and transform the Minkowski metric into a Euclidean-form complex bilinear metric. The four Hadamard spatial sign vectors form a regular tetrahedron and appear simultaneously in the transformed Dirac and Maxwell operators. The Dirac matrices satisfy a Euclidean-form Clifford algebra and contain tetrahedral combinations of Pauli matrices, whereas the Riemann--Silberstein Maxwell matrices realize the corresponding spin-1 structure. A gauge-invariant QED Lagrangian is formulated in the same coordinates. In Fourier space, the Dirac and Maxwell systems are governed by the common invariant [MATH], while the complete Maxwell operator admits an exact rectangular Clifford-like factorization. The formulation is further extended to the weak-field Einstein--Dirac--Maxwell system. In harmonic gauge, the linearized gravitational field is governed by the same scalar wave operator [MATH], while gravitational corrections to the Dirac and Maxwell equations enter through the perturbed tetrad, spin connection, and curvature. This common principal-operator structure suggests shared spectral kernels and scalar-wave preconditioning for coupled field solvers.
tldr: The paper constructs a Hadamard-tetrahedral symmetric representation of Minkowski spacetime and derives Clifford-like factorizations for Dirac and Maxwell operators, with extensions to weak-field Einstein-Dirac-Maxwell systems.
motivation: To provide a symmetric representation of Minkowski spacetime that unifies Dirac and Maxwell operators via a normalized Hadamard transformation and imaginary time coordinate.
method: Combines a fourth-order Hadamard transform with an imaginary temporal coordinate to form complex coordinates, yielding tetrahedral sign vectors and Euclidean-form Clifford algebras for Dirac and Maxwell matrices.
result: The Dirac and Maxwell systems share a common invariant in Fourier space, the Maxwell operator admits an exact rectangular Clifford-like factorization, and the formulation extends to the linearized Einstein-Dirac-Maxwell system in harmonic gauge.
conclusion: The shared principal-operator structure suggests possibilities for spectral kernels and scalar-wave preconditioning in coupled field solvers, though the work remains within mathematical and gravitational physics rather than quantum information.

title: Wasserstein Stability, Couplings Across Volumes, And The $1+1/d$ Moment Thresholds In The Edwards--Anderson Model
authors: Mauris Chueng, Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quenched pressure of the nearest-neighbor Edwards--Anderson Ising model with free and periodic boundary conditions. First, we prove that the infinite-volume pressure is [MATH]-Lipschitz in the coupling law for the [MATH]-Wasserstein distance, yielding quantitative thermodynamic limits for spatially inhomogeneous disorder. Second, for periodic volumes, we prove that almost-sure convergence under every joint coupling of the finite-volume disorder arrays is equivalent to complete convergence of the one-volume pressure laws. Third, we prove that [MATH] guarantees this universal-coupling conclusion. We further show that this exponent is optimal among uniform power-moment assumptions: for every [MATH], there is a centered symmetric law with finite [MATH]-th moment for which canonical nested volumes converge almost surely, whereas independently resampled volumes with the same fixed-volume marginals converge in probability but not almost surely. Finally, in dimension one, we prove that the first-moment condition is also necessary for a finite limiting pressure.
tldr: A rigorous mathematical study of the quenched pressure in the classical Edwards–Anderson Ising spin glass, establishing Wasserstein Lipschitz continuity, coupling-based convergence criteria, and sharp moment thresholds for the disorder distribution.
motivation: The paper aims to make precise the thermodynamic limit of the Edwards–Anderson model and to determine how much control over the disorder distribution (measured via Wasserstein distance and coupling of volumes) is needed for almost-sure convergence of finite-volume pressures.
method: Probabilistic and functional-analytic techniques are used: Wasserstein-distance Lipschitz stability of the infinite-volume pressure, joint-coupling arguments comparing nested versus independently resampled disorder volumes, and power-moment assumptions on the disorder law, with a one-dimensional necessity result.
result: The pressure is proven Lipschitz in the coupling law, complete convergence of one-volume laws is shown equivalent to a.s. convergence under any joint coupling, and a 1+1/d moment exponent is established as optimal among uniform power-moment assumptions (with first-moment necessity in d=1).
conclusion: The work provides sharp, quantitative conditions under which finite-volume spin-glass pressures converge universally, contributing to the rigorous statistical mechanics of disordered systems rather than to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Explicit Full-Spark And Quantitatively Phase-Retrievable Gabor Windows Via Algebraic Perturbations
authors: Dongwei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit finite Gabor windows whose orbits are simultaneously full spark and phase retrievable. In every cyclic dimension, algebraic specialization preserves all Gabor minors while removing every zero of the self-ambiguity function, thereby resolving the explicit simultaneous- construction problem arising in finite nilpotent-group phase retrieval. We isolate the underlying regularization principle: a sufficiently small algebraic perturbation transfers full spark from one seed while retaining an ambiguity gap from another. In every prime dimension \(p\geq5\), this gives an explicit full-spark window with normalized ambiguity margin at least \(c_0p^{-1/2}\), for an absolute constant \(c_0>0\); the order is sharp by the finite Moyal identity. Chinese-remainder tensorization followed by the same regularization extends the \(N^{-1/2}\) scale to squarefree cyclic dimensions having a bounded number of prime factors. The resulting full-data lifted intensity map has a dimension-independent lower stability bound on each such family. A second explicit seed gives a polynomial ambiguity margin, of order \(N^{-2}\), in every cyclic dimension, and we prove that this order is sharp within the geometric-seed construction. We also identify why the sharper cubic-chirp argument itself cannot cross that boundary: the unmodified cubic chirp has systematic ambiguity zeros at every modulus \(p^a\), \(a\geq2\). For a smaller fixed character perturbation and \(p\geq2^{14}\), we additionally prove uniform stability after a fixed fraction of arbitrary erasures on each fixed two-atom Gabor subspace. This last statement is deliberately local to one two-atom subspace and does not compare signals supported on different pairs.
tldr: Constructs explicit finite Gabor windows that are both full spark and phase retrievable using algebraic perturbations, with quantitative ambiguity margins in prime and cyclic dimensions.
motivation: The explicit simultaneous construction of full-spark and phase-retrievable Gabor windows is an open problem in finite nilpotent-group phase retrieval.
method: Algebraic specialization/perturbation preserves all Gabor minors while removing zeros of the self-ambiguity function; Chinese-remainder tensorization extends results to squarefree cyclic dimensions.
result: In prime dimensions p≥5, yields full-spark windows with ambiguity margin ≥ c0 p^{-1/2} (sharp by Moyal identity); a second seed gives polynomial margin ~N^{-2} in every cyclic dimension, and uniform stability under erasures is proved for a fixed fraction on two-atom Gabor subspaces.
conclusion: The work resolves the explicit simultaneous-construction problem and identifies limits of the cubic-chirp argument, providing constructive tools for phase retrieval.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Joint Target Detection And Parameter Estimation - Characterizing Mixed-State Sensing Limits Via Posterior Entropy Volume
authors: Dazhuan Xu, Nan Wang, Han Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of integrated sensing and communication calls for a unified theoretical foundation for sensing. This paper models target-presence patterns and continuous physical parameters as a mixed discrete-continuous state [MATH] on a branched reference measure, and treats posterior entropy volume and joint mutual information as two complementary representations of the same limit. Entropy volume carries physical units, can be compared with engineering scales such as resolution cells, and remains meaningful when the number of active targets varies; mutual information is dimensionless, invariant to coordinates and units, and additive through the chain rule. We define entropy number, entropy volume, and mixed entropy volume for discrete, continuous, and mixed states, respectively. The maximum-entropy principle for the uniform distribution on a support of fixed measure explains the measure-theoretic meaning of the exponential entropy scale, while the main limit follows from a mixed asymptotic equipartition property and a posterior probability-volume inequality through conditional typical sets. For asymptotically reliable high-probability sensing regions, the minimum achievable first-order posterior mixed entropy volume equals the prior mixed entropy volume multiplied by [MATH], where [MATH]. Thus, detection and estimation contributions multiply in the volume domain and add in the bit domain, and one sensing bit halves the posterior effective measure. We further prove that posterior-preserving cascades attain the direct-inference limit, while arbitrary intermediate compression incurs the exact information loss [MATH]. Numerical results for a single-target presence-range model illustrate the information composition, posterior entropy-volume contraction, and cascade-interface loss.
tldr: This paper develops a unified information-theoretic framework for joint target detection and parameter estimation using posterior entropy volume and mutual information, with a mixed discrete-continuous state model.
motivation: Integrated sensing and communication requires a unified theoretical foundation for sensing that jointly captures discrete target presence and continuous parameter estimation.
method: The authors model target-presence patterns and continuous parameters as a mixed discrete-continuous state on a branched reference measure, define entropy number, entropy volume, and mixed entropy volume, and prove limits via a mixed asymptotic equipartition property and a posterior probability-volume inequality.
result: For asymptotically reliable sensing regions, the minimum achievable first-order posterior mixed entropy volume equals the prior mixed entropy volume multiplied by a factor, showing that detection and estimation contributions multiply in volume domain and add in bit domain, and that one sensing bit halves the posterior effective measure.
conclusion: The framework provides fundamental limits for joint detection and estimation and clarifies information loss in cascaded sensing systems, with numerical illustrations for a single-target presence-range model.

title: Topological Instability And Reentrant Crystallization In Active Solids
authors: Zory Davoyan, Aditya Jha, Anton Souslov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the KTHNY theory of defect-mediated melting in two dimensions to the case of active solids exhibiting both non-reciprocal (odd) elasticity and Cosserat (micropolar) coupling. For perturbatively small values of non-reciprocity, melting still proceeds via defect unbinding, but the melting temperature shifts due to activity. However, at a threshold value of non-reciprocity, we discover a qualitatively distinct mechanism for 2D melting, which we call topological instability. This melting occurs through the proliferation of defect pairs at any temperature. We use a combination of field theory and simulations to characterize this zero-temperature transition in terms of the defect-pair fugacity. Surprisingly, for higher activity values, we find reentrant crystallization, where the quasi-long-range order survives even at temperatures for which the equilibrium crystal would melt. Although active solids present one realization of this topological instability, we envision core-energy-driven defect proliferation as a generic and unexplored route for two-dimensional melting.
tldr: The paper extends KTHNY melting theory to active solids with odd elasticity and Cosserat coupling, predicting a topological instability and reentrant crystallization.
motivation: Two-dimensional melting in active solids is not well understood, especially when non-reciprocal and micropolar effects are present.
method: The authors combine field theory with simulations, using defect-pair fugacity to characterize a zero-temperature transition.
result: Beyond a threshold non-reciprocity, defect pairs proliferate at any temperature, causing a topological instability; at higher activity, quasi-long-range order can survive at temperatures that would melt equilibrium crystals.
conclusion: Core-energy-driven defect proliferation is proposed as a generic route to 2D melting, with active solids as one realization.

title: MiNCE: Nonparametric, Strongly Consistent Confidence Envelopes For Band-Limited Functions And Their Smoothed Spectra
authors: B\'alint Horv\'ath Bal\'azs Csan\'ad Cs\'aji
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimum-norm confidence envelope strategies offer a nonparametric approach to constructing nonasymptotic, simultaneous confidence regions for band-limited functions, exploiting the theory of Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS). While the finite-sample coverage guarantees of these envelopes have been established, their consistency has not been analyzed so far. In this paper, we study this construction, here termed the Minimum-Norm Confidence Envelope (MiNCE) framework, and establish the strong uniform consistency of the resulting bands, both for noise-free and noisy observation models, under mild assumptions on the measurement noises. We further extend this formulation to the frequency domain, deriving nonasymptotic, simultaneous, strongly uniformly consistent confidence bands for the smoothed spectra. Numerical experiments in nonparametric regression and spectral estimation empirically confirm our theoretical results, illustrating the contraction of the confidence envelopes toward the target function as the sample size increases.
tldr: The paper establishes strong uniform consistency for nonparametric minimum-norm confidence envelopes for band-limited functions and their smoothed spectra.
motivation: Minimum-norm confidence envelopes provide nonasymptotic simultaneous confidence regions for band-limited functions using RKHS theory, but their consistency had not been analyzed.
method: The authors analyze the MiNCE framework and prove strong uniform consistency for noise-free and noisy observation models, extending the construction to frequency-domain confidence bands for smoothed spectra.
result: They derive nonasymptotic, simultaneous, strongly uniformly consistent confidence bands and empirically demonstrate contraction of envelopes toward the target function in nonparametric regression and spectral estimation.
conclusion: The MiNCE framework yields strongly consistent confidence envelopes for band-limited functions and smoothed spectra, supported by numerical experiments.

title: A Discrete Mellin Calculus In The Toeplitz Algebra
authors: Georgios Stylogiannis Carlo Bellavita
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the classical Ces\`aro operator belongs to the Toeplitz algebra, providing an independent solution to a question raised by Barr\'ia and Halmos. Our approach is based on a discrete Mellin calculus for the sampled-ratio matrices \[ W(\kappa)_{jk} = {j+1}\, \kappa\!\left({j+1}\right). \] For a natural algebra of kernels [MATH], we prove that this quantization is multiplicative modulo Hilbert--Schmidt operators, \[ W(\kappa)W(\eta) - W(\kappa \star \eta) \in S_2, \qquad \kappa,\eta \in A. \] We further show that every operator [MATH], [MATH], belongs to the commutator ideal of the Toeplitz algebra. Since the Ces\`aro operator corresponds to the kernel [MATH], this resolves the Barr\'{\i}a--Halmos question as a special case of the general framework.
tldr: The paper develops a discrete Mellin calculus to show that the Cesàro operator belongs to the Toeplitz algebra, resolving a question of Barría and Halmos.
motivation: The work is motivated by a classical operator-theoretic question about whether the Cesàro operator lies in the Toeplitz algebra, and by the desire for a general framework for sampled-ratio matrices.
method: The authors introduce a discrete Mellin calculus for sampled-ratio matrices W(kappa), prove multiplicativity modulo Hilbert-Schmidt operators for a natural algebra of kernels, and show that certain operators lie in the commutator ideal of the Toeplitz algebra.
result: They establish that W(kappa)W(eta) - W(kappa star eta) is Hilbert-Schmidt and that the Cesàro operator corresponds to a particular kernel, giving an independent solution to the Barría-Halmos question.
conclusion: The paper provides a new algebraic perspective on the Toeplitz algebra via discrete Mellin calculus, with the Cesàro operator case as a special instance.

title: A Convergent Reaction-Drift-Diffusion Master Equation With Interaction Potentials
authors: Samuel A. Isaacson Max Heldman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the convergent reaction-diffusion master equation (CRDME) framework on unstructured grids to include two-body interaction potentials between particles. Such interactions are essential for modeling systems in which particles experience electrostatic repulsion, volume exclusion, or van der Waals attraction. Our approach discretizes the weak form of the forward equation for a particle-based stochastic reaction- drift-diffusion model to obtain a new CRDME by combining two complementary techniques: an edge- averaged finite element method with mass-lumping quadrature for spatial transport terms that include potential interactions, and a mix of finite volume and mass-lumping quadrature approximations for reaction terms. This yields transition rates for a spatial jump process of particles hopping between dual mesh voxels and undergoing reactions. The resulting spatially discrete CRDME retains key physical properties of the continuum system in closed domains. It preserves the Gibbs-Boltzmann equilibrium distribution in the absence of reactions, and satisfies detailed balance of both drift-diffusion and reactive fluxes for systems with reversible reactions. Numerical comparisons with Brownian dynamics simulations validate our method, and we demonstrate empirical second-order convergence as the mesh is refined.
tldr: The paper extends the convergent reaction-diffusion master equation (CRDME) to include two-body interaction potentials on unstructured grids, yielding a spatially discrete jump process that preserves equilibrium and detailed balance.
motivation: Interaction potentials such as electrostatic repulsion, volume exclusion, and van der Waals attraction are essential for accurately modeling particle-based stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, but existing CRDME frameworks lack them.
method: The authors discretize the weak form of the forward equation using an edge-averaged finite element method with mass-lumping quadrature for transport terms and a combination of finite volume and mass-lumping approximations for reactions, producing transition rates for particle hopping and reactions.
result: The resulting CRDME preserves the Gibbs-Boltzmann equilibrium distribution in closed domains without reactions, satisfies detailed balance for reversible reactions, and shows empirical second-order convergence when compared to Brownian dynamics simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a convergent mesoscopic model for reaction-diffusion systems with interaction potentials, bridging particle-based and master-equation descriptions.

title: Uniform Chebyshev Approximations Of Functions Satisfying A Variation-type Condition: Reconstruction Of Time-varying Signals On Graphs
authors: Davide Bianchi, Sandra Saliani, Dimitrios Vavitsas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove uniform approximation theorems for Chebyshev expansions of continuous functions of two variables. Under a variation-type condition on the square [MATH], a continuous function admits a uniformly convergent Chebyshev expansion in the first variable whose coefficients are continuous functions of the second variable. These results are applied to the spectral graph wavelet transform of time-varying signals on finite weighted graphs: the scaling and wavelet kernels are approximated by expansions with time-varying coefficients whose degrees do not depend on time, the composition of the approximate transform with its adjoint admits the same explicit coefficient formulas as in the time-independent case, and reconstruction by the pseudoinverse is stable, with explicit bounds in terms of the uniform kernel errors. Numerical experiments on a sensor network confirm the convergence and stability estimates. In a denoising problem, soft thresholding of the graph wavelet coefficients with a time-varying transform parameter improves over its time-independent, fixed-parameter counterpart.
tldr: The paper proves uniform Chebyshev approximation theorems for two-variable functions and applies them to time-varying spectral graph wavelet transforms, achieving stable reconstruction and improved denoising.
motivation: To extend spectral graph wavelet transforms to time-varying signals on graphs by providing theoretical guarantees for approximation and reconstruction when kernels vary with time.
method: The authors prove uniform convergence of Chebyshev expansions under a variation-type condition, then use these to approximate time-varying scaling and wavelet kernels with time-independent degrees, and analyze the stability of pseudoinverse reconstruction.
result: The approximate transform and its adjoint retain explicit coefficient formulas from the time-independent case, reconstruction is stable with explicit bounds in terms of kernel errors, and numerical experiments on a sensor network confirm convergence and stability; soft thresholding with a time-varying parameter improves denoising over the fixed-parameter counterpart.
conclusion: The framework enables efficient and stable processing of time-varying graph signals with theoretical guarantees, with potential applications in sensor networks and beyond.

title: Classification Of Finite-dimensional Nichols Algebras Of Rank Two In Twisted Yetter--Drinfeld Categories
authors: Bowen Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite non-abelian group, let \(\Phi\in Z^3(G,\mathbb C^\times)\) be normalized, and let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional simple objects of \({}_G^G^{\Phi}\). We classify, up to interchange, the braided-indecomposable pairs \((V,W)\) whose supports generate \(G\) and for which \(\mathcal B(V\oplus W)\) is finite-dimensional. The classification consists of eight cases with five possible support quandles. In every case the Cartan graph is standard of type \(A_2\), \(B_2\), or \(G_2\), and the dimension is determined explicitly. A new phenomenon occurs for \(\Gamma _2\): the twisted setting admits a family of type \(G_2\) absent from the ordinary \(\Gamma _2\) classification and we construct an explicit example over a non-abelian group of order \(16\).
tldr: This paper classifies finite-dimensional rank-two Nichols algebras in twisted Yetter-Drinfeld categories, identifying eight cases with standard Cartan graphs and a new type G2 phenomenon.
motivation: Nichols algebras are central to the classification of pointed Hopf algebras and quantum groups, and the twisted Yetter-Drinfeld setting extends known results from ordinary categories.
method: The authors work with a finite non-abelian group G, a normalized 3-cocycle Φ, and simple objects V,W of the twisted category, classifying braided-indecomposable pairs whose supports generate G and for which the Nichols algebra of V⊕W is finite-dimensional.
result: They obtain eight cases with five possible support quandles, all Cartan graphs of type A2, B2, or G2, and explicitly determine dimensions; a new family of type G2 appears in the twisted setting, with an explicit example over a non-abelian group of order 16.
conclusion: The classification shows that twisting can produce Nichols algebras absent from the ordinary case, revealing richer structure in twisted Yetter-Drinfeld categories.

title: Compute-Bounded Security Assurance - Coverage, Verification, And Response Under Resource Constraints
authors: Ditto PS Jithin VG
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Additional inference compute can increase the number of correctly resolved security-assurance tasks, but repeated success, unique coverage, accepted evidence, and operational protection are different quantities. We develop a resource-constrained framework that separates them. For repeated conditionally independent attempts with latent success probability [MATH], coverage is [MATH], and its limiting value is [MATH]. Positive pairwise outcome correlation does not by itself imply a ceiling below one: we construct two models with the same mean success and pairwise correlation but different limiting coverage. We distinguish this result from the effective sample size used to estimate a mean, and show why finite-budget observations cannot generally identify an asymptotic support ceiling. We then connect coverage to fallible evidence checking, proper scoring of factual grounding, complete resource accounting, service capacity, and a response model that includes mitigation delay. A conceptual defensive architecture separates evidence analysis, adjudication, and operational authority. An evaluation protocol specifies held-out tasks, paired comparisons, negative cases, and uncertainty reporting. The contribution is a consistent theoretical synthesis and a set of counterexamples to invalid extrapolations, rather than an empirical scaling law. All numerical illustrations are analytic; no model-parity result, hardware benchmark, or general attacker-defender equilibrium is claimed.
tldr: The paper proposes a resource-constrained framework for security assurance that distinguishes coverage, verification, and operational response under compute limits.
motivation: Increased inference compute can improve security-assurance task success, but repeated success, unique coverage, accepted evidence, and operational protection are different quantities that require separate treatment.
method: It develops analytic models for coverage under repeated conditionally independent attempts, connects coverage to fallible evidence checking and proper scoring, and outlines a defensive architecture with an evaluation protocol.
result: Pairwise outcome correlation does not imply a coverage ceiling below one, and finite-budget observations generally cannot identify an asymptotic support ceiling; the contribution is theoretical synthesis and counterexamples rather than an empirical scaling law.
conclusion: The work offers a conceptual framework and cautions against invalid extrapolations in compute-bounded security assurance, with no claims of model parity or hardware benchmarks.

title: Cross User/App Network Attacks - Hijacking Tcp Connections And Dns Cache Poisoning Via A Malicious User/App (Extended Version)
authors: Amit Klein Tamir Shahar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Off-path network attacks against TCP and DNS (over UDP) client-server connections are generally considered impractical nowadays, due to built-in security features in these protocols, e.g. randomized TCP (initial) sequence numbers and randomized UDP source ports, respectively. In this work, we refute this presumption by demonstrating that an unprivileged malicious application running on the client (but practically off-path), when combined with a remote off-path adversary, can enable powerful network attacks against such connections. We show how such a local--remote collaboration between the malicious application and a remote adversary allows inference of sensitive connection state, including TCP sequence numbers and DNS stub-resolver UDP source ports. Our attacks exploit standard socket API calls such as bind(), protocol mechanisms such as IP options, and operating system features such as cBPF and procfs to infer the TCP initial sequence number (ISN) and the UDP source port in use by the connection of interest. Specifically, we take advantage of certain properties of the ISN generation algorithm as implemented in major operating systems. We demonstrate TCP connection hijacking in Linux, Android, Windows, macOS and iOS, and DNS cache poisoning against Windows, Android and the popular systemd-resolved DNS stub resolver in Linux. We evaluate our techniques across multiple operating systems and realistic deployment settings, including environments behind port-preserving NAT-integrated routers. We disclosed our techniques to Microsoft, Apple, Linux and Google, which led to the release of several patches.
tldr: A malicious local application combined with a remote off-path adversary can infer TCP sequence numbers and DNS source ports to hijack connections and poison DNS caches across major operating systems.
motivation: Off-path TCP and DNS attacks are considered impractical due to randomized sequence numbers and source ports; the authors challenge this by exploiting local-remote collaboration.
method: The attack uses standard socket API calls like bind(), IP options, cBPF, and procfs to leak the TCP initial sequence number and UDP source port from the client, enabling off-path inference.
result: The authors demonstrate TCP connection hijacking on Linux, Android, Windows, macOS, and iOS, and DNS cache poisoning against Windows, Android, and systemd-resolved, leading to vendor patches.
conclusion: The paper refutes the presumed impracticality of off-path attacks and shows that unprivileged local malware can enable powerful network attacks against TCP and DNS.

title: Concept Drift Mitigation Through Community And Spectral Graph Analysis For The Detectionof Cyberattacks In Network Traffic
authors: Julien Michel, Abdul Qadir Khan, Majed Jaber, Pierre Parrend
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In network traffic, legitimate behaviours and attack techniques evolve jointly - the phenomenon known as 'concept drift' [1]. Every detector is thereby left obsolete between two updates, and always one step behind adversaries. In this work, we propose to move the point of intervention from the model, repaired after the drift, to the feature space, selected before learning. We therefore introduce t-robustness, a stability score defined for each feature independently of any detection model, comparable across an entire feature space. It combines the step-by-step distance between successive statistical states of a feature, and its cumulative divergence from its initial state, so that a slow monotonic drift cannot pass for stability. The candidates are drawn from abnormal network connectivity patterns left by scans, DoS and communications between endpoints, read through graph community metrics and spectral metrics. The evaluation is performed on the UGR16 dataset, across three learning scenarios and a control scenario, as well as without model update, and demonstrate that t-robust feature spaces sustain detection where the baselines collapse: retained expectancy at the last test interval reaches 0.6025, against 0.5230 for graph community features and 0.3831 for the base NetFlow features.
tldr: The paper introduces t-robustness, a model-independent feature stability score using graph community and spectral metrics to mitigate concept drift in network traffic cyberattack detection.
motivation: Legitimate and malicious network behaviours evolve jointly, causing concept drift that makes detectors obsolete between updates.
method: It defines t-robustness for each feature by combining step-wise statistical state distances and cumulative divergence from an initial state, and selects robust features from abnormal connectivity patterns via graph community and spectral metrics.
result: On the UGR16 dataset, t-robust feature spaces sustain detection better than baselines: retained expectancy at the last test interval reaches 0.6025 versus 0.5230 for graph community features and 0.3831 for base NetFlow features.
conclusion: Moving intervention from post-drift model repair to pre-learning feature selection, guided by t-robustness, improves cyberattack detection under concept drift.

title: Intermittent Continuous-time Random Walks Under Renewal Reset Mechanism
authors: Guohua Li, Hong Zhang, Yuexiong Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic resetting as a practical and efficient search strategy in complex and disordered environments has long been a topic of interest to researchers. Based on the competition between jumping and resetting, this article proposes and investigates intermittent continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) under stochastic resetting, using the smaller waiting time for jump and reset as the renewal time, where the waiting times for both jump and reset can have arbitrary distributions. After each renewal event, the system will proceed with new waiting times for jump and reset regardless of their previous histories. We study the governing equation and Montroll-Weiss equation with renewal resetting, as well as the Markovian resetting for intermittent CTRWs. We prove the existence of non-equilibrium stationary states within the renewal reset mechanism when the jump and reset waiting times follow any exponential and power law distributions. For exponential and Gaussian distributed jump lengths, we examine the mean square displacements (MSDs) of particles to determine their monotonicity and asymptotic stability. Moreover, we calculate the first-arrival time to quantify search efficiency, and validate the intermittent CTRWs under renewal resetting lead to a finite mean first-arrival time (MFAT) to any fixed position for exponential jump and reset waiting time distributions (WTDs), power-law jump and exponential reset WTDs, as well as exponential jump and power-law reset WTDs. However, the MFAT diverges for power-law jump and reset WTDs. The intermittent CTRW model, which is based on the competition mechanism, can be applied to many physical scenarios, such as the foraging strategy of animals that return to their nests after an unsuccessful foraging attempt, or the work planning of intelligent robots that return to energy replenishment points after prolonged operation.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes intermittent continuous-time random walks under a renewal reset mechanism where jump and reset waiting times compete, deriving stationary states, mean square displacements, and mean first-arrival times.
motivation: Stochastic resetting is an efficient search strategy in complex environments, and combining it with intermittent continuous-time random walks may better model scenarios such as animal foraging and robot recharging.
method: Using renewal theory and Montroll-Weiss equations, the authors study governing equations for arbitrary jump and reset waiting-time distributions, including exponential and power-law cases, and compute MSDs and MFATs.
result: Non-equilibrium stationary states exist for exponential and power-law waiting-time distributions; MFAT is finite for several combinations of jump and reset distributions but diverges when both follow power laws.
conclusion: The competition-based intermittent CTRW model provides a framework for search processes with resetting and can be applied to biological foraging and robotic work planning.

title: The Diophantine Equation $p^{x}+6^{y}=z^{2n}$: A Complete Solution For Half Of The Primes
authors: Pagdame Tiebekabe
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a prime number and let [MATH] be an integer. We completely solve the exponential Diophantine equation [MATH] in positive integers [MATH] for every prime [MATH] such that the Legendre symbol [MATH] equals [MATH], that is, for [MATH]: the equation has no solution, with the single exception [MATH]. Since these residue classes contain half of all primes in the sense of Dirichlet density, this settles the equation for one prime out of two, uniformly in the exponent [MATH]. Two ingredients of the proof have independent interest. First, we show that the Ramanujan--Nagell type equation [MATH] has no solution with [MATH], using Zsigmondy's theorem on primitive prime divisors; this removes the extra congruence hypotheses that appeared in earlier work of the author on the case [MATH] and solves the open problems formulated there. Secondly, we prove that [MATH] has [MATH] as its unique solution, thereby completely resolving the exceptional prime. The Legendre condition is sharp: we exhibit solutions for primes with [MATH] realising each branch of the factorisation argument. All results are corroborated by extensive computational verification, and we state several open problems, including the complete classification of the solutions when [MATH].
tldr: The paper completely solves the exponential Diophantine equation p^x + 6^y = z^{2n} for half of all primes, using Zsigmondy's theorem and resolving several Ramanujan–Nagell type cases.
motivation: The author aims to settle open cases of an exponential Diophantine equation and remove earlier congruence hypotheses, thereby advancing classical number theory.
method: The proof combines Legendre-symbol conditions, factorization arguments, Zsigmondy's theorem on primitive prime divisors, and computational verification to handle Ramanujan–Nagell type equations.
result: For primes with (some Legendre symbol) equal to a specified value, the equation has no positive integer solutions except one exceptional prime; the exceptional case is fully resolved, and the Legendre condition is shown to be sharp.
conclusion: The work provides a uniform solution for half of the primes in the sense of Dirichlet density and states open problems for remaining cases, but it is purely number-theoretic and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Stability Of Fork-Join Systems With Redundancy And Heterogeneous Servers
authors: Chutong Gao, Seyed Iravani, Ohad Perry
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the stability problem of fork-join systems with redundancy (FJR) and heterogeneous servers under both static and dynamic capacity-allocation policies. In an [MATH] FJR system, each arriving job is split into [MATH] independent tasks, with one task assigned to each of [MATH] parallel servers. Once [MATH] tasks have been processed, they are joined and the corresponding job departs the system; the remaining [MATH] unprocessed tasks are then removed and are therefore termed redundant. We first identify the nominal traffic intensity and characterize the maximal stability region, defined as the set of traffic intensities for which there exists an admissible policy that stabilizes the system. We then establish conditions under which this maximal stability region is attained for two classes of policies: static and dynamic. Specifically, we show that for static allocation policies, in which service capacities remain fixed over time, maximality is achieved whenever the fastest server is allocated no more than [MATH] of the total service capacity. For dynamic allocation policies, in which a fixed total service capacity may be repeatedly reallocated among the servers, we show that maximality is achieved whenever the cumulative capacity allocated to the [MATH] shortest queues does not exceed [MATH] of the total capacity for every [MATH]. Our analysis is based on a projection of the [MATH] FJR system onto a simpler [MATH] system that has no redundancy, together with a novel sample-path comparison argument for multidimensional processes based on the generalized Schur-convex order.
tldr: This paper studies stability conditions for fork-join queueing systems with redundant task processing and heterogeneous servers under static and dynamic capacity allocation.
motivation: Fork-join systems with redundancy are important in modern distributed computing and cloud systems, where replicating tasks can reduce latency but complicates stability analysis.
method: The authors project the redundant fork-join system onto a simpler non-redundant system and develop a sample-path comparison argument for multidimensional processes using the generalized Schur-convex order.
result: They characterize the maximal stability region and show that static policies attain it when the fastest server gets no more than a certain fraction of total capacity, while dynamic policies attain it under a cumulative capacity condition on the shortest queues.
conclusion: The work provides sharp stability criteria for heterogeneous redundant fork-join systems, with implications for capacity allocation in distributed computing.

title: Optimality Of Kl{\o}ve Arrays Within The Symmetric Kl{\o}ve-Mossige Class
authors: Hongwei Zhao Lilin Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rajam[MATH]ki and Koivunen asked whether minimum-redundancy symmetric Kl[MATH]ve-Mossige arrays with contiguous sum co-arrays are always Kl[MATH]ve arrays. We give a computer-assisted proof that, at every fixed sensor count, every maximizing sensor set belongs to the Kl[MATH]ve class. The argument classifies the overlaps between a generator and its shifted reflection, then bounds the aperture of a hypothetical optimizer outside the Kl[MATH]ve class. Comparing these bounds with a classical Kl[MATH]ve construction settles all sensor counts at least 330. An exact integer certificate covers the remaining counts from 2 through 329 and matches every equality case to a Kl[MATH]ve array as a complete set. Consequently, optimization within the full symmetric Kl[MATH]ve-Mossige class reduces to the previously known search over Kl[MATH]ve parameters. The theorem concerns this specified class, rather than unrestricted sparse arrays or all restricted additive bases.
