tldr: The paper gives a computer-assisted proof that optimal symmetric Kløve-Mossige arrays with contiguous sum co-arrays always belong to the Kløve class for any fixed sensor count.
motivation: Rajamäki and Koivunen asked whether minimum-redundancy symmetric Kløve-Mossige arrays with contiguous sum co-arrays are always Kløve arrays.
method: The authors classify overlaps between a generator and its shifted reflection, bound the aperture of a hypothetical optimizer outside the Kløve class, and supplement the argument with an exact integer certificate for small sensor counts.
result: They settle all sensor counts at least 330 by comparison with a classical Kløve construction and cover counts 2 through 329 with an exact certificate that matches every equality case to a Kløve array.
conclusion: Optimization within the full symmetric Kløve-Mossige class reduces to the previously known search over Kløve parameters, for the specified class rather than unrestricted sparse arrays or all restricted additive bases.

title: Complex Numbers: Uncommon Knowledge
authors: Ivan Penkov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we unveil some subfields of the field of complex numbers which are well known to specialists, but seem to remain hidden for a wider mathematical audience. The existence and construc- tions of these fields follow directly from famous results of the 20-th century, however standard graduate textbooks avoid these topics.
tldr: A short expository note collecting lesser-known subfields of the complex numbers that arise from classical 20th-century results but are omitted from standard graduate textbooks.
motivation: Many interesting subfields of the complex numbers are known to specialists but remain unfamiliar to a broader mathematical audience because standard textbooks skip them.
method: Expository survey, presenting existence proofs and explicit constructions of these subfields derived from well-known 20th-century theorems.
result: Several subfields of the complex numbers are exhibited along with their constructions, drawn from classical results in field theory and algebra.
conclusion: The note aims to make these specialist-level facts about complex number subfields more widely accessible to mathematicians.

title: Stable Coexistence In Ecologies And Games
authors: T\"urk\"u \"ozl\"um \c{c}elik, Vincenzo Antonio Isoldi, Irem Portakal, Giulio Zucal
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study feasible stable equilibria of Lotka-Volterra systems and their higher-order extensions. We complete the classification of impossible ecological interaction networks with at most four species and extend several of these impossibility results to families with arbitrarily many species. We then show that these sign-pattern obstructions are specific to the pairwise Lotka-Volterra model: arbitrary prescribed growth rates and pairwise coefficients can be supplemented by higher-order interactions so as to admit a feasible asymptotically stable equilibrium. Through the correspondence with replicator dynamics, we interpret feasible equilibria of higher-order Lotka-Volterra systems as totally mixed symmetric Nash equilibria of symmetric multiplayer games, derive bounds on their number, and study their robustness under perturbations of the payoff tensors. We conclude by showing that every impossible ecology determines a nonempty open class of symmetric two-player games with no totally mixed evolutionarily stable strategy.
tldr: The paper classifies stable coexisting equilibria in Lotka-Volterra ecological systems and extends the analysis to higher-order interactions and symmetric multiplayer games.
motivation: Stable coexistence and impossibility results in ecological interaction networks are central to theoretical ecology and evolutionary game theory, but the role of higher-order interactions and connections to game-theoretic equilibria remain incompletely understood.
method: The authors use sign-pattern analysis and algebraic/geometric methods to classify impossible ecological networks with up to four species, extend impossibility results to larger families, and relate higher-order Lotka-Volterra equilibria to totally mixed symmetric Nash equilibria in multiplayer games.
result: They complete the classification for at most four species, show that higher-order interactions can stabilize otherwise impossible pairwise systems, derive bounds on the number of totally mixed symmetric equilibria, and construct open classes of symmetric two-player games without totally mixed evolutionarily stable strategies.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions fundamentally alter stability and coexistence beyond the pairwise Lotka-Volterra paradigm, with direct implications for multiplayer game theory and evolutionary stability.

title: On The Sequential Test And Distributed Detection
authors: Earnest Akofor
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a simple definition of stopping time and its role in the formulation of sequential tests for both centralized and distributed detection, providing a straightforward procedure for obtaining optimal decision rules. Upper bounds for optimal stopping time are derived and numerically shown to possess certain qualitative features expected of the optimal stopping time. The results are extended to any distributed detection network in the form of an acyclic directed graph.
tldr: The paper formulates sequential tests for centralized and distributed detection using a simple stopping-time definition, derives upper bounds on optimal stopping time, and extends the framework to detection networks represented as acyclic directed graphs.
motivation: The work aims to provide a straightforward procedure for obtaining optimal decision rules in sequential and distributed detection problems.
method: It defines stopping time and uses it to formulate sequential tests, derives upper bounds for optimal stopping time, and generalizes the results to distributed detection networks described by acyclic directed graphs.
result: Numerical examples show that the derived upper bounds exhibit qualitative features expected of the optimal stopping time.
conclusion: The framework offers a simple approach to sequential and distributed detection with potential applicability to graph-structured detection networks.

title: Degree Sequence Reconstruction From Subgraph Traces
authors: Venkata Gandikota, Arick Grootveld, Haodong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of degree sequence reconstruction is to recover the ordered vector of degrees of an unknown graph from vertex deleted traces, where each vertex is deleted independently with probability [MATH]. We provide two algorithms for reconstruction; the first uses rejection sampling to reduce the problem to an estimation problem for a mixture distribution. Combined with prior trace reconstruction results, this gives a reconstruction algorithm using [MATH] traces, although no sub-exponential time decoder is known. Our other approach involves recovering certain graph invariants, degree moments, that can identify a graphs degree sequence. Extremal polynomial bounds show that [MATH] degree moments are necessary and sufficient to reconstruct the degree sequence, which leads to an algorithm with [MATH] trace complexity. The same polynomial machinery yields a sub-exponential time decoder for the degree sequence from the moments. Additionally, we give an [MATH] upper bound and a [MATH] lower bound for the trace complexity of recovering the number of edges.
tldr: The paper studies reconstruction of a graph's degree sequence from vertex-deleted subgraph traces, providing algorithms and bounds for trace complexity and moments.
motivation: Degree sequence reconstruction from subgraph traces is a classical graph-theoretic inverse problem with connections to trace reconstruction and combinatorics.
method: Two algorithms are proposed: one reduces the problem to mixture-distribution estimation via rejection sampling, while the other recovers degree moments using extremal polynomial bounds and a sub-exponential decoder.
result: The first approach yields a reconstruction algorithm using exponentially many traces, and the second achieves polynomial trace complexity while also giving upper and lower bounds for recovering the number of edges.
conclusion: The work advances classical graph reconstruction theory but has no apparent connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Afterimage Slow Regions In First-Order Methods For Linear Conic Programming
authors: Heng Yang Shucheng Kang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-order methods for linear conic programming often stall on long plateaus. Existing analyses characterize when during a run or on which problem instances slow convergence occurs; we instead ask where in the state space slow convergence is present. We introduce the slow region family for parameterized averaged fixed-point iterations. On a slow region, one step moves the state by only a small fraction of its distance to the fixed-point set, so an orbit starting there keeps almost its initial distance for arbitrarily many iterations. We then develop the afterimage principle to construct them. A center family and a nearby petal family share the same limit parameter, so their residual fields become close, while their fixed-point sets or forward drifts stay far apart. The petal geometry then certifies a slow region for the center. We verify the standing assumptions for ADMM, sGS-ADMM, and PDHG, and give an LP, SOCP, and SDP gallery showing how varied slow regions can be.
tldr: The paper introduces 'slow regions' for parameterized averaged fixed-point iterations and develops an 'afterimage principle' to construct them, explaining where in state space first-order conic programming solvers like ADMM and PDHG stall.
motivation: First-order methods for linear conic programming often exhibit long plateaus, and existing analyses only characterize when in a run or on which instances slow convergence occurs, leaving the question of where in the state space slowness arises unaddressed.
method: The authors define a family of slow regions for averaged fixed-point iterations where a single step reduces the distance to the fixed-point set by only a small fraction, and prove an afterimage principle that constructs such regions by comparing a center family with a nearby petal family sharing the same limit parameter.
result: The construction certifies slow regions via petal geometry, and the standing assumptions are verified for ADMM, sGS-ADMM, and PDHG, with an LP, SOCP, and SDP gallery demonstrating the variety of slow regions.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric, state-space-based account of slow convergence in first-order conic optimization, complementing existing convergence-rate and instance-based analyses.

title: Constructive Tchakaloff Results And Well-conditioned Quadrature Through Randomized Least Squares
authors: Filip B\v{e}l\'{i}k, Akil Narayan, John Turnage
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider using randomized least squares to construct quadrature rules exact on a subspace of functions. Using new conditions that we call relative admissibility and reference weight concentration, we establish both that the quadrature weights from such a procedure concentrate close to their asymptotic values with prescribed and arbitrarily large probability, and this in turn provides useful finite-sample probabilistic bounds on the stability of the resulting quadrature rules for very general classes of possibly complex-valued functions. Our analysis both significantly generalizes the existing analysis of randomized least squares quadrature construction, and provides new bounds on stability for these rules. These results specialize to existence results for positive quadrature rules, when such rules can be theoretically expected. Because our procedures are formally algorithmic, our analysis is a substantive advance toward computationally constructive generalized Tchakaloff theorems.
tldr: The paper develops randomized least squares methods for constructing stable quadrature rules, with probabilistic bounds and constructive generalized Tchakaloff results.
motivation: Classical quadrature construction and Tchakaloff theorems often rely on non-constructive existence arguments or lack finite-sample stability guarantees.
method: The authors introduce relative admissibility and reference weight concentration conditions and analyze randomized least squares to build quadrature rules exact on a subspace.
result: They obtain high-probability concentration of quadrature weights near asymptotic values and finite-sample stability bounds for broad classes of complex-valued functions, yielding positive quadrature existence results.
conclusion: The work significantly generalizes prior randomized least squares quadrature analysis and advances computationally constructive generalized Tchakaloff theorems.

title: Oracle Complexity Of Stochastic Fixed-Point Equations With Nonexpansive Maps
authors: Jelena Diakonikolas, Crist\'obal Guzm\'an, David Mart\'inez-Rubio
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the oracle complexity of computing a point with small fixed-point residual [MATH], for a general norm [MATH] and a self-map [MATH] of a compact convex set. We study this problem in the setting where [MATH] is nonexpansive with respect to the same norm [MATH] and accessed via an unbiased stochastic oracle with bounded variance [MATH]. We provide an algorithm that solves such instances for any norm with a weak Rademacher type [MATH], with high probability. The algorithm is based on a recursive anchoring technique. For type-[MATH] spaces, such as [MATH]-spaces for [MATH], our algorithm attains stochastic oracle complexity [MATH]. We further prove a near-matching lower bound (i.e., matching up to poly-log factors) for such [MATH]-norm instances in high dimensions. Our lower bound holds against any randomized algorithm that succeeds with constant probability. It further extends to settings with ``sparse'' noise, where variance measured with respect to any [MATH] norm is of the same order, ruling out the possibility of improving oracle complexity as a function of [MATH] by measuring variance in a non-matching [MATH] norm.
tldr: The paper establishes matching upper and lower bounds on the stochastic oracle complexity of finding approximate fixed points of nonexpansive maps in general normed spaces.
motivation: Fixed-point computation for nonexpansive maps underlies many optimization and equilibrium problems, but the optimal oracle complexity in arbitrary norms with stochastic first-order information was not well characterized.
method: The authors introduce a recursive anchoring algorithm that works for any norm with weak Rademacher type, and derive near-matching complexity lower bounds for type-p spaces via randomized-algorithm arguments, including extensions to sparse noise settings.
result: The algorithm achieves stochastic oracle complexity at the expected order for type-p normed spaces such as L_p for p in (1,2], and a poly-log-matching lower bound is proven to hold in high dimensions against any randomized algorithm succeeding with constant probability.
conclusion: The results pin down the oracle complexity of stochastic nonexpansive fixed-point problems and rule out improvements from measuring variance in a non-matching norm.

title: An Intrinsic Finite Element Framework For Scalar- And Vector-valued Partial Differential Equations On General Manifolds
authors: Tamara A. Tambyah, Alberto F. Mart\'in, David Lee, Santiago Badia
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an intrinsic finite element framework for the numerical approximation of scalar- and vector-valued partial differential equations on general manifolds described by atlases of charts. Weak formulations and their discretisation are expressed exclusively in the flat parametric space of the manifold, where the exact geometry enters only through the metric tensor that is evaluated at quadrature points. Conforming finite element spaces of arbitrary order for the whole de Rham complex are obtained on multi-chart atlases through purely topological inter-chart gluing. We develop a nodal change of basis construction for vector-valued spaces on multi-chart atlases, where nodal degrees of freedom couple charts with incompatible coordinate systems through transmission maps. Inter-chart continuity holds at the nodes with jumps of the order of the approximation error, and the resulting discrete field is exactly tangent to the manifold. Optimal convergence rates for this method are observed numerically for the surface Stokes problem; no a priori error analysis is provided. Numerical experiments on the cubed sphere manifold in two and three dimensions for the Hodge Laplacian problems demonstrate the intrinsic framework is free of the geometric consistency errors for a sufficient quadrature degree, and that intrinsic assembly is substantially cheaper than its extrinsic counterpart. Further considering the rotating shallow water equations that include orography as a perturbation of the geometry demonstrates that mass is conserved exactly, and energy is conserved up to the time discretisation error.
tldr: The paper introduces an intrinsic finite element framework for solving scalar- and vector-valued PDEs on general manifolds using multi-chart atlases and metric-tensor-based weak formulations.
motivation: Numerical methods for PDEs on curved manifolds typically suffer from geometric consistency errors and expensive extrinsic assembly; a chart-based intrinsic formulation aims to avoid these issues.
method: Weak formulations and discretizations are expressed purely in the flat parametric space, with exact geometry entering only via the metric tensor at quadrature points, and conforming de Rham complex spaces constructed through topological inter-chart gluing and nodal change-of-basis transmission maps.
result: Numerical experiments on the cubed sphere for Hodge Laplacian problems show optimal convergence, freedom from geometric consistency errors at sufficient quadrature degree, cheaper intrinsic assembly, and exact mass conservation (energy conserved up to time discretization) for rotating shallow water equations.
conclusion: The intrinsic finite element framework provides an efficient, geometry-robust approach to manifold PDEs, though no a priori error analysis is provided.

title: Heavy-Ball Method Under Randomized Schedules
authors: Shuzhong Zhang Chang He
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how predefined randomized parameter schedules accelerate the heavy-ball method on general smooth convex objectives. Our analysis distinguishes two levels of randomization: sampling gradient-evaluation times within intervals whose boundaries are deterministic, and additionally randomizing the time boundaries themselves. With deterministic time boundaries, we construct fixed-time and anytime schedules that achieve an expected last-iterate function value gap of order [MATH]; the anytime schedule also satisfies the same rate almost surely. We then use randomized time boundaries and obtain the improved last-iterate rate [MATH], both in expectation and almost surely. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first global nonasymptotic convergence guarantee for the heavy-ball method on general smooth convex functions that improves polynomially over the classical [MATH] rate. Our result shows that the heavy-ball method achieves a strictly better convergence rate than the best known result [MATH] attainable by plain gradient descent with silver stepsize schedules.
tldr: The paper derives the first global nonasymptotic convergence guarantees for the heavy-ball optimization method under randomized parameter schedules, showing polynomial improvement over the classical rate on smooth convex objectives.
motivation: Acceleration of first-order optimization methods is a central question in convex optimization, and the heavy-ball method's convergence behavior under general smooth convex functions has lacked tight global guarantees.
method: The authors analyze two levels of randomization—sampling gradient-evaluation times within deterministic intervals and randomizing the interval boundaries themselves—to construct fixed-time and anytime schedules for the heavy-ball method.
result: Randomized schedules achieve expected last-iterate gaps that improve polynomially over the classical rate, with the anytime variant holding almost surely; the random-boundary version yields a strictly better rate than the best known gradient descent with silver stepsize schedules.
conclusion: Randomized scheduling provides a principled route to accelerated heavy-ball convergence, establishing the method as strictly faster than plain gradient descent in the studied setting.

title: Proportional-limit Asymptotics For Diaconis-Ylvisaker-penalised Logistic Regression With Fitted Intercept
authors: Philipp Sterzinger
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops estimator-level asymptotic theory for maximum Diaconis-Ylvisaker prior penalised likelihood for logistic regression with a jointly fitted intercept and nonzero prior slope direction in the proportional-limit regime. For [MATH] Gaussian covariates and [MATH], a conditional convex Gaussian min--max analysis yields almost-sure convergence of the fitted intercept and a pseudo-Lipschitz empirical law for the slope estimator. This estimator-level law gives asymptotic limits for out-of-sample scores, classification error, optimal thresholding and oracle calibration. It also yields oracle-adjusted fixed-block [MATH]-statistics under isotropic Gaussian covariates, and yields the main ingredient in establishing the limiting distribution of the penalised likelihood-ratio test statistic and identifies the rescaling to recover the nominal chi-square distribution. We extend these results to Gaussian designs with arbitrary deterministic mean and positive-definite covariance via affine centering and whitening and discuss extensions to subgaussian covariates. Finally, we propose a consistent response-moment estimator of the oracle parameters entering the state equations that govern the slope limiting law and are required for feasible inference.
tldr: This paper develops estimator-level asymptotic theory for Diaconis-Ylvisaker-penalised logistic regression with a fitted intercept in the proportional-limit regime.
motivation: Classical asymptotic theory for penalised logistic regression often fails in high-dimensional proportional-limit settings where the number of covariates scales with sample size, motivating a finer estimator-level analysis.
method: A conditional convex Gaussian min-max (CGMT) analysis is applied to Gaussian covariates, yielding almost-sure convergence of the fitted intercept and a pseudo-Lipschitz empirical law for the slope estimator, extended to general Gaussian designs via affine centering and whitening.
result: The derived laws give asymptotic limits for out-of-sample scores, classification error, optimal thresholding, oracle calibration, fixed-block statistics, and the limiting distribution of the penalised likelihood-ratio test statistic with its chi-square rescaling.
conclusion: The authors also propose a consistent response-moment estimator of the oracle parameters entering the state equations, enabling feasible inference in this asymptotic regime.

title: Encrypt What Matters: When Selective Homomorphic Inference Is Efficient
authors: Ali Backour, Juan Reyes, Jaime Punyed, Ana Onoprishvili
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables inference on private data without revealing it to the server, but evaluating an entire input under FHE is expensive. We study , where only a sensitive region of interest (ROI) is encrypted, and computations independent of that region are performed in plaintext. Selective evaluation produces the same output as full FHE on the same model, without retraining. Its efficiency depends on how quickly encrypted dependencies spread through the network. For small encrypted ROIs, locality-preserving architectures can achieve order-of-magnitude homomorphic-evaluation speedups, whereas architectures with early global mixing provide essentially no speedup. These results identify locality as the key architectural property governing the benefit of selective homomorphic inference.
tldr: This paper studies selective homomorphic inference where only a sensitive region of interest is encrypted, showing that locality-preserving neural architectures enable order-of-magnitude speedups compared to architectures with early global mixing.
motivation: Fully homomorphic encryption allows private inference but is computationally expensive when applied to entire inputs. The authors aim to reduce this cost by encrypting only the sensitive parts of the input and performing the rest of the computation in plaintext.
method: They analyze how encrypted dependencies spread through a model when only a region of interest is under FHE, comparing locality-preserving architectures against those with early global mixing, and measure homomorphic-evaluation speedups without retraining.
result: For small encrypted ROIs, locality-preserving architectures achieve order-of-magnitude speedups in homomorphic evaluation, while architectures with early global mixing provide essentially no speedup.
conclusion: Locality is identified as the key architectural property governing the benefit of selective homomorphic inference, offering a practical path to efficient privacy-preserving inference.

title: Audio Deepfake Detection Using Temporal Coherence Analysis
authors: Sarah Barrington Justin D. Norman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proliferation of AI-generated audio (so-called "deepfake" audio) poses significant threats to information integrity, from voice cloning fraud to synthetic music copyright disputes. We present a temporal coherence analysis framework built upon Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining (CLAP) embeddings that spans speech, instrumental music, and music with vocals. By computing pairwise cosine similarities between audio segment embeddings and extracting statistical features from the resulting distributions, we train lightweight ensemble classifiers that reliably distinguish authentic from synthetic audio. Our work provides an interpretable, computationally efficient alternative to common deep learning methods while still achieving competitive performance across speech and music domains. Further, we reveal two notable empirical findings about audio deepfakes: (1) a feature-label inversion phenomenon in which 21 of 29 statistical features reverse their discriminative direction between training and in-the-wild deployment, and (2) a speech--music direction reversal in which entropy discriminates in opposite directions for speech and music deepfakes.
tldr: The paper presents a temporal coherence analysis framework using CLAP embeddings and lightweight classifiers to detect audio deepfakes across speech and music domains.
motivation: The proliferation of AI-generated audio poses threats to information integrity, motivating an interpretable and computationally efficient detection method.
method: It computes pairwise cosine similarities between audio segment embeddings from CLAP, extracts statistical features from the resulting distributions, and trains ensemble classifiers.
result: The framework achieves competitive performance on speech and music, and reveals two empirical phenomena: feature-label inversion in deployment and a speech–music direction reversal in entropy discrimination.
conclusion: The approach offers an interpretable, efficient alternative for audio deepfake detection while highlighting domain-specific generalization challenges.

title: Scalable Composition Of Byzantine Agreements Under Reorder Attacks
authors: Jing Chen, Jin Dong, Jichen Li, Xuanzhi Xia, Wentao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Byzantine agreement (BA) is a foundational building block in distributed systems, and the security analysis of BA protocols under multi-instance executions has attracted increasing attention. However, most existing adversary models focus solely on party corruption and neglect important threats posed by adversarial manipulations of communication channels in the network. Through channel attacks, messages can be reordered across multiple executions and lead to violations of the protocol's security guarantees, In this work, we present the first adversary model that combines party corruption and channel attacks. Based on this model, we establish new security thresholds for Byzantine agreement under parallel and concurrent compositions, supported by complementary impossibility and possibility results that match each other to form a tight bound. For the impossibility result, we show that even authenticated Byzantine agreement protocols cannot be secure under parallel composition when [MATH] or [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] denote the number of corrupted parties and communication channels, respectively, and [MATH] is the number of parties. For the possibility result, we prove the existence of secure protocols for unauthenticated Byzantine agreement under parallel and concurrent composition, when [MATH]. We first provide general black-box compilers that transform any single-instance secure BA protocol into one that is secure under parallel and concurrent executions without additional security assumptions. To optimize performance, we further design refined compilers using erasure-correcting codes. These refined versions significantly reduce communication overhead, particularly for long messages, where they achieve a constant multiplicative overhead compared with the original protocol, thus achieving the same asymptotic communication complexity.
tldr: The paper introduces a Byzantine agreement adversary model combining party corruption and channel reordering attacks, establishing tight security thresholds for parallel and concurrent composition.
motivation: Existing Byzantine agreement analyses typically consider only corrupted parties and ignore adversarial manipulation of communication channels, which can break security under composed executions.
method: The authors define a combined adversary model and prove matching impossibility and possibility results, then construct black-box and erasure-code-based compilers for secure composition.
result: They show authenticated BA cannot be secure under parallel composition for certain corruption/channel thresholds, while unauthenticated BA can be secure for a broader range, with refined compilers achieving constant communication overhead.
conclusion: The work provides a tight characterization of Byzantine agreement security under channel reordering and scalable compilation techniques, advancing classical distributed systems rather than quantum information.

title: Session Attestation For Unmodified Tls Services In Confidential Virtual Machines
authors: Sheng Ma Qi Gu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential virtual machines simplify the migration of existing services into trusted execution environments, yet attesting their network connections often requires changing applications, TLS implementations, or certificates. We present SessionLatch, which provides session attestation while preserving all three. The key insight is that a trusted observation of the server's locally generated ephemeral public key, combined with standard TLS key confirmation, establishes the TEE endpoint guarantee without accessing TLS secrets. This moves attestation integration to the operating system: a temporary latch holds client encrypted records while evidence exchange overlaps the application TLS handshake, then removes itself after verification. The resulting connection retains enterprise service authentication and the native TLS data path, with no additional payload encryption. Mutual attestation uses the same construction and overlaps evidence generation at both endpoints. We implement Linux andWindowsintegrationandevaluaterealHygonCSVattestation. SessionLatch reduces short-upload mean latency by 63.1%/23.0% relative to TNG in interleaved Linux/Windows experiments. These results show that session attestation can strengthen existing confidential services without making a permanent proxy part of their data path.
tldr: SessionLatch provides TLS session attestation for confidential virtual machines without modifying applications, TLS implementations, or certificates by latching encrypted records during evidence exchange.
motivation: Attesting network connections in confidential VMs typically requires invasive changes to applications, TLS stacks, or certificates, which hinders adoption and complicates migration of existing services.
method: The approach observes the server's locally generated ephemeral public key and uses standard TLS key confirmation to establish a TEE endpoint guarantee without accessing TLS secrets; a temporary OS-level latch holds client encrypted records while attestation evidence is exchanged during the handshake.
result: Implemented on Linux and Windows with Hygon CSV attestation, SessionLatch reduced short-upload mean latency by 63.1% and 23.0% relative to TNG in interleaved Linux/Windows experiments while preserving native TLS data paths and enterprise authentication.
conclusion: Session attestation can strengthen existing confidential services without permanently inserting a proxy into the data path, but the work is in classical confidential computing and does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Subgroup Membership Inference Audits Of Differentially Private Synthetic Text
authors: Yidan Sun, Viktor Schlegel, Srinivasan Nandakumar, Siew Kei Lam, Anil Anthony Bharath
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic data releases are increasingly proposed in the literature as a means of sharing realistic data replicas in lieu of sensitive private datasets. Even when the worst-case privacy leakage of such releases is bounded by means of differential privacy (DP), in practice a residual risk remains. Membership inference attack (MIA) audits are conducted to empirically quantify this risk. However, existing methods only measure average-case risk for randomly drawn records, which might conceal the risk to vulnerable subgroups. To highlight this issue, we define a subgroup-targeted membership inference game in which the target pool is an explicit parameter, and instantiate it with an audit of 32 proxies under three scenarios with different levels of attacker knowledge, across four datasets, three generators (DP-SGD fine-tuning, API-based prompting, and activation steering), and five privacy budgets. The audit shows that synthetic releases leak subgroup membership and that prior attacks systematically underestimate this leakage. DP is effective at the aggregate level: it substantially reduces average leakage at every budget we test. Three observations temper this picture. First, the remaining leakage is concentrated rather than spread out: under DP, a tenth of the records carries roughly 40% of it. Second, the protection DP delivers in practice is uneven: within its worst-case guarantee, the noise removes more of the measured leakage from random records than from high-risk ones---and a merged-pool audit that scores both record types against shared negatives confirms this at the record level. Third, records leak proves to be a property of the release mechanism rather than of the record alone, so record-level risk cannot be assessed independently of the release.
tldr: The paper introduces a subgroup-targeted membership inference audit to quantify residual privacy leakage in differentially private synthetic text releases, showing existing average-case audits underestimate risk to vulnerable subgroups.
motivation: Synthetic data releases bounded by differential privacy still carry residual membership inference risk, and existing audits measure only average-case risk for randomly drawn records, potentially concealing disproportionate leakage for vulnerable subgroups.
method: The authors define a subgroup-targeted membership inference game with the target pool as an explicit parameter and instantiate it via 32 proxy attacks under three attacker-knowledge scenarios, spanning four datasets, three generators (DP-SGD fine-tuning, API prompting, activation steering), and five privacy budgets.
result: Synthetic releases leak subgroup membership and prior attacks systematically underestimate it; under DP the residual leakage is concentrated (a tenth of records carry ~40%), and DP's practical protection is uneven, removing more leakage from random records than from high-risk ones.
conclusion: Record-level privacy risk is a property of the release mechanism rather than the record alone, so it cannot be assessed independently of the release, motivating subgroup-aware auditing practices.

title: Fast Collision-Free Acquisition In 1-Persistent Age-Threshold Slotted Aloha Via Role-Protected Counters
authors: Pl\'inio Santini Dester
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goal-oriented sensing, estimation, and control benefit from prompt, regular access to task-relevant updates. Although 1-persistent age-threshold slotted ALOHA (1-pTSA) can self-organize into a periodic collision-free schedule, its acquisition transient can dominate finite-horizon performance. We propose role-protected counter-threshold slotted ALOHA (RP--CTSA), which separates reservation memory from the age of information (AoI). A scheduled singleton retains its phase after colliding with active contenders, whereas a collision involving multiple scheduled nodes releases them immediately; AoI resets only after a decoded update. The protocol requires individual acknowledgments and a binary RELEASE/HOLD indication, but no centralized phase assignment or identification of colliders. Let [MATH] denote the number of nodes and [MATH] the counter threshold. Under inverse-population access scaling, the acquisition dynamics admit an exact pure-death representation. When [MATH], the acquisition time is [MATH]; when [MATH], with [MATH], it is [MATH]. Simulations confirm both regimes and show substantial finite-horizon AoI gains over 1-pTSA while preserving every collision-free schedule.
tldr: The paper proposes role-protected counter-threshold slotted ALOHA to accelerate collision-free acquisition in age-threshold random access networks.
motivation: Goal-oriented sensing and control require timely updates, but the acquisition transient of 1-persistent age-threshold slotted ALOHA can dominate finite-horizon performance.
method: The protocol separates reservation memory from Age of Information (AoI) using role-protected counters and binary RELEASE/HOLD feedback, avoiding centralized phase assignment or collider identification.
result: Under inverse-population access scaling, acquisition dynamics admit an exact pure-death representation with analytic acquisition-time regimes, and simulations show finite-horizon AoI gains over 1-pTSA while preserving collision-free schedules.
conclusion: RP-CTSA improves initial access speed and AoI performance in slotted ALOHA networks, but the contribution is entirely classical and outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: AutoTrans: AI-Assisted Automatic Translation Of Security Assertions For Risc-v Processors
authors: Sharjeel Imtiaz, Uljana Reinsalu, Tara Ghasempouri
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusing a set of verified security assertions across RISC-V processor targets remains one of the most expensive bottlenecks in hardware security verification. Manual translation takes hours per assertion. Raw LLM translation is fast but unreliable, introducing signal hallucination, where the model invents port names absent from the target RTL and produces outputs that may vary across model updates or even within the same model version. This paper presents AutoTrans, an automated framework that addresses the above shortcomings. First, a new lightweight Regular Expression-based System Verilog signal extractor is proposed to identify the signals for generating security assertions. This step is necessary to prevent signal hallucination. Second, a template is introduced to create prompt and pinned inference parameters that guarantee a byte-identical prompt assembly on every run, making the pipeline output resilient to model updates. Moreover, the introduced template for LLM prompting is capable of generating security assertions from English-only security descriptions of RISC-V processors, with no manual authoring. Third, a formal verification process (JasperGold FPV) is integrated, which guarantees that the generated security assertions verify the security of the RISC-V processor rather than silently entering the result set. The workflow is applied on Deepseek V4 to translate security assertions from one RISC-V to another (e.g., for IBEX from NS31A RISC-V). The experiment shows that AutoTrans achieves 78\% Auto Translation Acceptance Rate (TAR) automatically and without human intervention and 100\% Final TAR after refinement by humans.
tldr: AutoTrans is an LLM-based framework that automatically translates hardware security assertions from one RISC-V processor to another, using regex-based signal extraction, deterministic prompt templating, and formal verification to eliminate signal hallucination.
motivation: Reusing verified security assertions across different RISC-V processor targets is a major bottleneck in hardware security verification, since manual translation takes hours per assertion while raw LLM translation is fast but unreliable and prone to hallucinating non-existent signal names.
method: The framework combines a lightweight regex-based SystemVerilog signal extractor to ground the model in real port names, a pinned prompt template and inference parameters ensuring byte-identical prompt assembly across runs, and an integrated JasperGold formal property verification (FPV) step to ensure generated assertions actually verify the target processor.
result: Applied to DeepSeek V4 for translating assertions (e.g., from NS31A to IBEX RISC-V cores), AutoTrans achieved a 78% automatic Translation Acceptance Rate with no human intervention, rising to 100% final TAR after human refinement.
conclusion: The work shows that structured, deterministic LLM prompting combined with signal grounding and formal verification can make automatic security-assertion translation practical for RISC-V hardware verification, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Distributed And Private Textual Data Synthesis From Embeddings
authors: Ergute Bao, Hongyan Chang, Ali Shahin Shamsabadi, Ting Yu, Xiaokui Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit differentially private (DP) text synthesis in the realistic setting of distributed users, where privacy concerns preclude a trusted curator with access to raw user texts. Existing DP text synthesis pipelines are designed for a trusted, centralized curator and often cannot be deployed in distributed settings due to unrealistic trust and access assumptions; when adapted naively, they require repeated, tightly synchronized user participation and incur significant overhead. To address this gap, we propose a DP--cryptography co-design for textual data synthesis that requires no trusted curator and requires only lightweight user participation. Our approach has two optimized components. First, we design a distributed-friendly DP synthesis algorithm that releases a one-time DP summary in an embedding space: it identifies frequent semantic regions and releases their DP centroids, enabling training-free, non-iterative offline text synthesis. We further introduce semantic support protection, which ensures the released summary avoids semantic neighborhoods of infrequent texts, reducing the risk of exposing rare user data. Second, we develop a custom secure protocol that implements this algorithm over distributed user data, enforcing end-to-end DP guarantees without requiring a trusted curator. On four benchmarks, we achieve utility comparable to the state-of-the-art centralized DP synthesis method.
tldr: The paper proposes a distributed differentially private text synthesis framework that releases a one-time DP summary in embedding space, avoiding a trusted curator and enabling training-free offline text generation.
motivation: Existing DP text synthesis methods assume a trusted centralized curator, which is unrealistic in distributed settings where users must retain control over raw text data.
method: It combines a distributed-friendly DP synthesis algorithm that identifies frequent semantic regions and releases DP centroids with a custom secure protocol enforcing end-to-end DP guarantees without a trusted curator.
result: Across four benchmarks, the method achieves utility comparable to state-of-the-art centralized DP synthesis while requiring only lightweight user participation.
conclusion: The work shows that privacy-preserving text synthesis can be performed effectively in distributed settings without a trusted curator, using embedding-space summaries and cryptographic co-design.

title: Sound Debloating Of Redundant Checks In Zero-Knowledge Machine-Learning Circuits
authors: Zhantong Xue, Pingchuan Ma, Zhaoyu Wang, Yuguang Zhou, Huaijin Wang, Shuai Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-knowledge (ZK) proof systems for neural-network inference compile the model into a system of arithmetic constraints. Many of these constraints are redundant checks: range proofs, sign lookups, and bit decompositions who are globally entailed by the rest of the circuit through chains of reasoning that span distant gadgets. Removing them shrinks the circuit and accelerates proving, but the removal must be carefully justified: an unsoundly debloated circuit becomes forgeable, accepting witnesses the original would have rejected and so allowing a prover to claim, for example, that a neural network produced an output it never actually computed. Such soundness vulnerabilities are not hypothetical: under-constrained circuits in deployed ZK systems have enabled attackers to forge transactions and bypass verification entirely. We present an automated framework that removes redundant checks while provably preserving soundness. For each candidate removal, our tool first checks whether the rest of the circuit, on its own, can still rule out every value the removed check was excluding. Using whole-circuit abstract interpretation, the analysis searches for such alternative justifications and records them in a provenance graph; a check is then removed only when an alternative path through the graph still derives the facts that it is checking. This ensures that the debloated circuit opens no new forging strategy to an adversary. We evaluate circuits spanning MLP, CNN, RNN, and transformer architectures generated by two production frameworks (ezkl and zkml), with up to 25.3 million constraints. Our tool removes up to 48.7\% of constraints and reduces prover time by up to 72.8\%, without weakening security.
tldr: An automated framework removes redundant constraints from zero-knowledge machine-learning circuits while provably preserving soundness.
motivation: Redundant range proofs, sign lookups, and bit decompositions inflate ZK circuit size and prover time, but naive removal can make circuits forgeable.
method: The tool applies whole-circuit abstract interpretation to find alternative justifications for each candidate check, records them in a provenance graph, and removes a check only when the remaining circuit still derives the excluded facts.
result: On MLP, CNN, RNN, and transformer circuits up to 25.3 million constraints, it removes up to 48.7% of constraints and reduces prover time by up to 72.8% without weakening security.
conclusion: Sound debloating of ZKML circuits can substantially improve proving efficiency while maintaining cryptographic soundness, addressing a practical vulnerability class in deployed ZK systems.

title: Identifiability Of Latent Space Network Models On Anisotropic Thurston Geometries
authors: Regina Ruane Marios Papamichalis
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A latent space network model places the nodes in a metric space and lets the probability of a tie decrease with distance. In a space of constant curvature, pairwise distances determine the positions up to an isometry. In the products and in the three remaining three-dimensional model geometries they do not. We study the three geometries that are neither of constant curvature nor products: the Heisenberg group, the solvable group and the universal cover of the unit tangent bundle of the hyperbolic plane. We ask what one network identifies about positions in them and when their geometry is detectable. Two anchors remove the isometry ambiguity. Small configurations are not determined by their distances, and generic local identification holds beyond a finite threshold, certified in the Heisenberg group. We derive the posterior on the quotient by the isometry group. For small configurations, the divergence to the nearest product or constant-curvature competitor is the stress component of the curvature difference and vanishes at high order in the scale; undirected ties therefore detect the geometry only in large networks with large enclosed areas. Directed ties expose it at first order: in the two twisted geometries, asymmetric preferences circulate around triangles in proportion to enclosed area, which no additive ranking produces. On dense competitive-game counter networks, the coupled model beats rankings on every geometry, degree-corrected rankings and free antisymmetric terms. A Euclidean model with the same coupled term matches it, so the gain is the coupling of similarity and circulation through shared coordinates. An additive-and-multiplicative-effects model predicts better still.
tldr: The paper studies identifiability and geometry detection in latent space network models built on anisotropic Thurston geometries (Heisenberg, solvable, and universal cover of the unit tangent bundle of the hyperbolic plane).
motivation: Latent space network models often assume constant-curvature or product geometries, but many non-Euclidean geometries leave pairwise distances insufficient to determine node positions; the authors ask what network structure reveals about positions and geometry in these anisotropic spaces.
method: They analyze two-anchor identifiability, derive posterior distributions on the quotient by the isometry group, and compare competitors via divergence expansions; they also test coupled similarity-circulation models on dense competitive-game counter networks.
result: Undirected ties detect geometry only in large networks with large enclosed areas, while directed ties expose it at first order through area-proportional asymmetric circulation; a coupled model outperforms rankings and free antisymmetric terms but is matched by a Euclidean model with the same coupling.
conclusion: Geometry detection in these anisotropic Thurston spaces requires directed ties or large-scale structure, and the key gain comes from coupling similarity and circulation through shared coordinates rather than from the non-Euclidean geometry itself.

title: Renewal Process's Guide To Fractional Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: Hong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Navier-Stokes equations, which remain unsolved, are crucial equations in fluid mechanics. Discovering the solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations is one of the challenging Millennium problems. In 1900, Hilbert proposed a potential approach to tackle this problem by establishing the relationship between microscopic dynamics and the macroscopic continuum equations. The key bridge is the derivation of Boltzmann equation and the theory of probability. In this paper, we shall use the collision renewal process with arbitrarily distributed waiting times to derive the Boltzmann equation for the time evolution of the probability of the velocity and the displacement of the particle, based on which we prove that the renewal process with exponential collision waiting time is equivalent to the classical Navier-Stokes equations, and that with power-law waiting time is equivalent to the fractional Navier-Stokes equations. Since the collision renewal process with arbitrarily distributed waiting times is a random process and is easy to perform the stochastic simulations of trajectories to obtain the corresponding solution, we actually find a stochastic approach to solve the classical and fractional Navier-Stokes equations.
tldr: The paper derives classical and fractional Navier-Stokes equations from a collision renewal process and proposes a stochastic simulation approach to solve them.
motivation: The Navier-Stokes equations are central to fluid mechanics and one of the Millennium Prize problems, and Hilbert suggested linking microscopic dynamics to macroscopic continuum equations.
method: The authors model particle motion via a collision renewal process with arbitrarily distributed waiting times and derive the Boltzmann equation for the velocity and displacement probability.
result: They show that exponential collision waiting times correspond to the classical Navier-Stokes equations, while power-law waiting times yield fractional Navier-Stokes equations.
conclusion: This provides a stochastic trajectory-based method for solving both classical and fractional Navier-Stokes equations.

title: Power Quasinormal Operators And The Root Problem
authors: Shihai Yang Jing-Bin Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct an [MATH]-power quasinormal operator [MATH] such that [MATH] is not quasinormal for some positive integer [MATH], thereby providing a counterexample to \cite[Lemma 3.1]{ko-filomat-2023}. We then investigate the relationships among the [MATH]-power quasinormality of [MATH], the normality of [MATH], and the quasinormality of [MATH], and show that these three conditions are equivalent in finite-dimensional spaces. We also provide a new proof that [MATH]-power quasinormal operators have the single-valued extension property \cite[Theorem 3.2]{ko-filomat-2023}; unlike the original proof, our argument does not rely on \cite[Lemma 3.1]{ko-filomat-2023} and thus closes the gap in the original argument. In addition, for a fixed operator [MATH], we characterize all positive integers [MATH] for which [MATH] is [MATH]-power quasinormal. As consequences, several results of Sid Ahmed are extended. Finally, we prove that every paranormal [MATH]-power quasinormal operator is quasinormal. Closely related to this, we also give an affirmative answer to the root problem of Stankovi\'c and Kubrusly \cite[Question 2.11]{stankovic-afa-2025}.
tldr: This paper studies power quasinormal operators in operator theory, constructs a counterexample to a known lemma, and resolves the root problem of Stanković and Kubrusly.
motivation: The work is motivated by correcting and extending results on power quasinormal operators, particularly a flawed lemma and related questions in operator theory.
method: The authors construct a specific power quasinormal operator as a counterexample, analyze equivalences between power quasinormality, normality, and quasinormality, and provide alternative proofs for the single-valued extension property.
result: They show the three conditions are equivalent in finite dimensions, characterize all powers for which an operator is power quasinormal, and prove that every paranormal power quasinormal operator is quasinormal.
conclusion: The paper closes a gap in the literature, extends Sid Ahmed's results, and gives an affirmative answer to the root problem of Stanković and Kubrusly.

title: On The Parameterized Complexity Of Coloring Discovery
authors: Sebastian Siebertz Eric Decker
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coloring Discovery asks whether a possibly improper initial coloring can be made proper within a prescribed number of allowed changes. We study the parameterized complexity of three modification step models that were studied previously in the literature: recoloring one vertex (color flipping), swapping the colors of arbitrary vertices (color swapping), and swapping colors only across an edge (color sliding). For color flipping, we give exact fixed-parameter algorithms for the parameters vertex cover and distance to complete. For color swapping, we obtain fixed-parameter tractability for the parameter vertex cover plus the number of colors. Our lower bounds show W[1]-hardness for treedepth plus feedback vertex set in the color flipping model and for the number of colors plus bandwidth or distance to disjoint paths in the swapping and sliding models. All three variants remain NP-complete with four colors on graphs of diameter two.
tldr: The paper studies the parameterized complexity of Coloring Discovery, where an improper coloring must be made proper with a bounded number of modification steps, under color flipping, swapping, and sliding models.
motivation: Coloring Discovery models graph modification problems where a coloring must be repaired under a budget of local operations, and its complexity landscape was previously only partially understood.
method: The authors design exact fixed-parameter algorithms for color flipping (parameterized by vertex cover and distance to complete), establish FPT results for color swapping with vertex cover plus number of colors, and prove W[1]-hardness lower bounds for several parameters.
result: FPT algorithms are given for vertex cover and distance-to-complete in the flipping model and for vertex cover plus color count in swapping; hardness holds for treedepth plus feedback vertex set, and for color count plus bandwidth or distance to disjoint paths. All variants remain NP-complete with four colors on diameter-two graphs.
conclusion: The work maps out the parameterized complexity boundaries of three coloring-repair models, showing a mix of tractability and intractability depending on the chosen parameterization.

title: Primal-Dual Inexact Newton-MR For Nonconvex Optimization With Equality Constraints
authors: Fred Roosta Oscar Smee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimization problems with nonlinear equality constraints arise throughout science, engineering, and increasingly in machine learning. Prominent methods for solving such problems include sequential quadratic programming and, more broadly, primal-dual Newton methods. Classical analyses of these methods typically rely on strong assumptions, perhaps most notably positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the null space of the constraint Jacobian. In practice, this assumption often necessitates strong regularization or the use of a positive definite Hessian surrogate. Moreover, in large-scale settings, solving the primal-dual Newton subproblem exactly is often computationally infeasible. To address these issues, we propose an inexact primal-dual Newton method with an inner solver based on the conjugate residual (CR) method. Exploiting recently established properties of CR, including negative-curvature detection, iterate monotonicity, and descent guarantees, our method handles indefiniteness in the subproblem directly as it arises. Our method thereby avoids detrimental regularization of the Lagrangian Hessian while naturally accommodating inexact solves. We establish worst-case global convergence guarantees and demonstrate strong empirical performance on large-scale, nonconvex problems.
tldr: This paper proposes an inexact primal-dual Newton method using the conjugate residual inner solver to solve nonconvex equality-constrained optimization problems without requiring positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian.
motivation: Classical primal-dual Newton methods rely on strong assumptions such as positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the null space of the constraint Jacobian, which often forces regularization, while exact subproblem solves become infeasible at large scale.
method: The authors develop an inexact primal-dual Newton method with a conjugate residual (CR) inner solver, exploiting CR's negative-curvature detection, iterate monotonicity, and descent guarantees to handle indefiniteness directly while allowing inexact solves.
result: They establish worst-case global convergence guarantees for the method and demonstrate strong empirical performance on large-scale nonconvex optimization problems.
conclusion: The approach avoids detrimental regularization of the Lagrangian Hessian and naturally accommodates inexact solves, offering a practical and theoretically grounded method for large-scale nonconvex constrained optimization.

title: Channel Estimation For Ofdm Via Delay-Doppler Refinement
authors: Mingcheng Nie, Hao Chang, Xiaoqi Zhang, Junkai Liu, Wibowo Hardjawana, Branka Vucetic, Yonghui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel channel estimation (CE) algorithm for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems that exploits the unique characteristics of the delay-Doppler (DD) domain channel. Specifically, the time-frequency (TF) domain input-output relationship (IOR) is derived in a compact form by focusing solely on the non-zero elements of the TF domain channel matrix. Based on this compact IOR, a coarse TF domain CE is first performed using a linear minimum mean square error estimator. Then, the resultant TF domain estimates are transformed to the DD domain through a unitary transformation for further refinement. We reveal that the effective DD domain channel matrix can be viewed as an aggregation of multiple DD domain channel responses with different phase shifts. This allows us to devise a threshold-based estimation for DD domain channel parameters with high accuracy. The estimated DD domain channel parameters are then applied to form a refined estimate of TF domain channel. Our numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve substantial performance gains over conventional OFDM channel estimation techniques under the same pilot deployment.
tldr: The paper proposes an OFDM channel estimation algorithm that refines coarse time-frequency estimates in the delay-Doppler domain using a threshold-based parameter estimator.
motivation: Conventional OFDM channel estimation performance is limited by pilot overhead and time-frequency domain sparsity assumptions, motivating exploitation of the delay-Doppler domain channel structure.
method: A compact time-frequency input-output relationship is derived, followed by LMMSE coarse estimation, unitary transformation to the delay-Doppler domain, and threshold-based refinement of delay-Doppler parameters to form a refined time-frequency estimate.
result: Numerical simulations show substantial performance gains over conventional OFDM channel estimation techniques under the same pilot deployment.
conclusion: The delay-Doppler refinement approach improves channel estimation accuracy for OFDM systems, though it is a classical wireless communications contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid systems relevance.

title: Learning-Aided Short Code Design For Isac Based On Mimo-ofdm
authors: Mingcheng Nie, Shuangyang Li, Geng Wang, Peng Cheng, Shenghong Li, Chang Liu, Giuseppe Caire, Yonghui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning (DL)-based coded waveform design for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), enabling flexible trade-offs between communication reliability and ranging accuracy in short-block transmissions. The proposed scheme is built upon a practical multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) architecture, where the communication channel state information and the angles of the static targets are assumed available at the transmitter. A transformer-based transmitter encodes input information bits directly into ISAC transmit waveforms to jointly optimize the bit error rate (BER) performance and the delay modified Cramer-Rao bound (MCRB). A corresponding transformer-based receiver is adopted at the communication side to recover the transmitted information bits. We further examine the learned codewords for communication-oriented and sensing-oriented designs, revealing that a balanced ISAC waveform naturally exhibits an intermediate structure between these two extremes. Numerical results illustrate these codeword structures and demonstrate that the proposed design provides substantial trade-off gains over conventional schemes based on standard channel coding and modulation.
tldr: This paper proposes a transformer-based deep learning framework for joint coded waveform design in MIMO-OFDM integrated sensing and communications (ISAC), balancing communication BER against sensing delay MCRB in short-block transmissions.
motivation: Short-block ISAC transmissions require flexible trade-offs between communication reliability and ranging accuracy, which conventional channel coding plus modulation schemes handle sub-optimally.
method: A transformer-based transmitter maps information bits directly into ISAC waveforms optimizing a joint BER/MCRB objective under a practical MIMO-OFDM architecture with known CSI and static target angles, paired with a transformer-based receiver for bit recovery.
result: Learned codewords for communication-oriented and sensing-oriented designs are examined, showing balanced ISAC waveforms exhibit an intermediate structure and yielding substantial trade-off gains over standard coded modulation baselines.
conclusion: Learning-aided end-to-end waveform design offers an effective means of navigating the communication-sensing trade-off in short-block MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems.

title: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning
authors: Thomas Rivasseau
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model safety and security research is preoccupied with, among other things, detecting and preventing jailbreak attacks: alignment bypasses that allow an adversarial user to elicit unwanted or harmful outputs from models. Arbitrary cipher, or covert communication, attacks are one such type of jailbreak and have previously been demonstrated against the fine-tuning APIs of commercial models. In these attacks, target models are trained on a corpus of encrypted harmful questions and responses and subsequently respond to harmful requests through the learned encryption scheme. In this paper, we show that newer frontier models do not require fine-tuning to acquire cipher-based communication skills. Instead, they can learn these skills through prompting and, when necessary, through in-context learning. Furthermore, model alignment is significantly weakened or entirely bypassed when communication occurs through the learned cipher. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes a novel attack vector against commercial black-box large language models. We demonstrate successful jailbreaks against frontier models developed by Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI. Our attack bypasses commercial harmfulness classifiers because harmful content is encrypted and therefore appears as nonsensical text or gibberish.
tldr: Frontier large language models can learn cipher-based covert communication purely through prompting or in-context learning, enabling jailbreaks that bypass safety alignment and harmfulness classifiers without any fine-tuning.
motivation: Prior arbitrary-cipher jailbreaks required training target models on corpora of encrypted harmful questions and responses via fine-tuning APIs, making them costly and limited to models with such access. The authors ask whether newer frontier black-box models can acquire cipher skills without fine-tuning.
method: The authors design cipher-based prompting and in-context learning attacks against commercial black-box frontier models from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, instructing models to communicate harmful content in learned or invented encryption schemes.
result: Models learn cipher communication through prompting alone, and alignment is significantly weakened or entirely bypassed when harmful content is encrypted; the attacks succeed against several frontier commercial models and evade harmfulness classifiers since the ciphertext appears as gibberish.
conclusion: Cipher-based covert communication constitutes a novel jailbreak vector against black-box LLMs that does not require fine-tuning, highlighting a gap in current safety alignment and content-classification defenses.

title: Lightweight Zero Trust Via Automotive Sdn
authors: Florian Wagner Friedrich Wiemer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zonal in-vehicle networks ship Ethernet, MACsec, and TSN, but treat the network itself as trusted: once configured at the factory, there is no standardized runtime way to easily revoke access, rotate keys, or contain a compromised ECU. Zero Trust Architecture targets exactly that gap, yet existing automotive ZTA proposals bolt on dedicated infrastructure that duplicates the SDN management plane already required to enable SDVs. Thus, ZTA is not yet adopted in the automotive domain, and the question remains: can we do better? We answer this in two steps. Step 1 analyses what Open Alliance TC17~v1.0 MACsec/MKA with pre-shared CAKs already provides in terms of NIST SP~800-207 ZTA tenets. Step 2 adds CORECONF/YANG management as proposed in Open Alliance TC19, maps the SDN Controller and Agents one-to-one onto NIST's PE, PA, and PEP. We then instantiate this with two YANG-based mechanisms: a network-access-control flow and a key-management scheme. The result fully covers five and two partially of the seven tenets with no ZTA-specific infrastructure added.
tldr: The paper proposes a lightweight zero-trust architecture for automotive zonal Ethernet networks by reusing existing MACsec/MKA and CORECONF/YANG SDN management rather than adding dedicated ZTA infrastructure.
motivation: Zonal in-vehicle networks assume the network is trusted after factory configuration, lacking runtime mechanisms to revoke access, rotate keys, or contain compromised ECUs, while existing automotive ZTA proposals duplicate SDN management planes already needed for software-defined vehicles.
method: The authors first map Open Alliance TC17 v1.0 MACsec/MKA with pre-shared CAKs onto NIST SP 800-207 ZTA tenets, then add TC19 CORECONF/YANG management, mapping the SDN Controller and Agents onto NIST's PE, PA, and PEP roles, and instantiate this with two YANG-based mechanisms for network access control and key management.
result: The combined approach fully satisfies five and partially satisfies two of the seven NIST ZTA tenets without introducing any ZTA-specific infrastructure.
conclusion: Zero-trust principles can be achieved in automotive networks by leveraging existing automotive Ethernet security and SDN management standards, avoiding redundant ZTA-specific deployments.

title: Energy Pathway Variety And The Progress Of The Energy Transition In European Countries
authors: Noam Abadi, Rossana Mastrandrea, Franco Ruzzenenti, Andrea Diaz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of new energy forms into existing energy infrastructure has emerged as a critical challenge in the context of the pursuit of a sustainable energy transition. One of the main challenges is understanding how this integration takes place not only from the introduction, but also as energy follows existing paths or creates new ones through which it is transformed and used by different activities. Here we introduce techniques from network science to analyse this process for the case of 29 European countries between 1992 and 2021. We study how new energy forms increase or decrease the variety (heterogeneity) of paths through the system of each country by establishing new ones and replacing or phasing out existing ones. We find that the transition to systems based on renewable energy is characterised by an initial increase in the variety of paths while the heterogeneity of paths decreases at the end of the transition, when the proportion of non-renewables in the system tends to zero. We then demonstrate that greater heterogeneity (complexity) is associated with larger annual fluctuations in the proportion of non-renewable sources in the system, establishing a direct relationship between the progress of the transition and the complexity of the energy system in which it occurs. This contributes to the understanding of general properties of the dynamics of the energy transition and effects that accelerate or deter it.
tldr: This paper uses network science to analyze how the variety and heterogeneity of energy pathways in 29 European countries evolved during the renewable energy transition from 1992 to 2021.
motivation: Understanding how new energy forms integrate into existing infrastructure—whether by following existing pathways or creating new ones—is crucial for managing sustainable energy transitions.
method: The authors construct energy pathway networks for each country and quantify path variety/heterogeneity, then relate these metrics to changes in the proportion of non-renewable energy sources over time.
result: The transition shows an initial increase in pathway variety followed by decreasing heterogeneity as non-renewables approach zero, and greater heterogeneity is associated with larger annual fluctuations in non-renewable share.
conclusion: The complexity of a country's energy system directly influences the dynamics and progress of its energy transition.

title: Counterexamples To Gns Conjecture 1.8
authors: Xiuqing Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove both parts of Conjecture 1.8 of Gabrielov, Novikov, and Shapiro (GNS). For the Coulomb potential, a generic rational configuration of 24 unit charges in [MATH] has at least 18 nondegenerate critical points of Morse index one but exactly 14 effective Voronoi one-cells. A separate proper-line construction has at least two nondegenerate minima but only one relatively effective zero-dimensional cell intersection. For each positive subspace dimension, product suspension gives a proper-subspace counterexample.
tldr: The paper disproves both parts of a conjecture by Gabrielov, Novikov, and Shapiro concerning critical points and Voronoi cells for Coulomb potentials.
motivation: The conjecture in question relates the number of nondegenerate critical points of Morse index one to the number of effective Voronoi one-cells for configurations of unit charges.
method: The author constructs explicit counterexamples, including a generic rational configuration of 24 unit charges and a separate proper-line construction, and uses product suspension to generalize to higher subspace dimensions.
result: For the Coulomb potential, a configuration of 24 unit charges yields at least 18 nondegenerate index-one critical points but exactly 14 effective Voronoi one-cells, and a proper-line construction gives at least two nondegenerate minima but only one relatively effective zero-dimensional cell intersection.
conclusion: Both parts of GNS Conjecture 1.8 are false, with counterexamples provided for each positive subspace dimension via product suspension.

title: Euler-Poincare Reduction: A Geometric Treatment Of The Relativistic Spinning Particle
authors: O. Teoman Turgut Burak Gul
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The heavy top is a classic example of Euler-Poincare reduction on a semidirect product group, demonstrating how an advected quantity-the direction of gravity-couples to rotational motion. While the description of relativistic spinning particles via Lie group configurations is well established in Hamiltonian (symplectic) mechanics, we demonstrate that an explicit Lagrangian Euler-Poincare reduction provides a direct, transparent parallel to the heavy top. Specifically, we show that the free relativistic spinning particle on the Poincare group is the precise Lorentzian analog of this system, with spacetime position being the advected quantity. This geometric unification not only illuminates the underlying symmetry of both systems but also clarifies why the introduction of external electromagnetic fields leads to a partial reduction. Finally, we establish that the transition to left-trivialized coordinates acts as a geometric selection mechanism, naturally favoring a class of interaction Lagrangians where spin-field coupling manifests as a dynamical redefinition of the particle's mass.
tldr: The paper applies Euler-Poincare reduction to the relativistic spinning particle on the Poincare group, drawing a geometric analogy with the heavy top.
motivation: The authors aim to provide an explicit Lagrangian Euler-Poincare reduction for the relativistic spinning particle, paralleling the heavy top system and clarifying the role of advected quantities and external fields.
method: They use geometric mechanics, specifically Euler-Poincare reduction on semidirect product groups, to formulate the free relativistic spinning particle as a Lorentzian analog of the heavy top.
result: The reduction shows that spacetime position is an advected quantity, external electromagnetic fields lead to partial reduction, and left-trivialized coordinates naturally select interaction Lagrangians with spin-field coupling as a dynamical mass redefinition.
conclusion: The work offers a transparent geometric unification of the heavy top and relativistic spinning particle, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Counting Type I And Type Ii Solutions Of The Erdos-Straus Equation: Concentration, Local Obstructions, And A Pointwise Comparison
authors: Xinyang Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a prime p >= 5 let f_I(p) and f_II(p) count the Type I and Type II solutions of the Erdos-Straus equation 4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z, in the sense of Elsholtz and Tao. We do not address the Erdos-Straus conjecture itself; our subject is the number of solutions. We turn a bijection of Bradford into an exact counting identity: f_I(p) and f_II(p) are sums, over the denominators n coprime to p, of the number of divisors of n^2 in a single residue class modulo e_n = 4n - p. A dual identity puts both counts on the same integer and the same modulus, distinguished only by the classes -p and -1. Our main unconditional result holds for every numerator m: the number of Type II solutions of m/p = 1/x + 1/(pY) + 1/(pZ) with Y <= K is at most sum_{n <= K} tau(n) = K log K + O(K), uniformly in p and m; on average over p <= N it is only O_m((log K)^3 log log K). Hence Type II solutions concentrate at x/p -> 1/m, while Type I solutions cannot. The numerator carries arithmetic information in two independent ways.
