A real character chi modulo e_n that is trivial on the primes dividing n annihilates Type II when chi(-1) = -1, and Type I when chi(-1)chi(m_0) = -1, where m_0 is the squarefree kernel of m; these coincide exactly when m is a square, so for the numerator 4 no criterion modulo squares can separate the two types. Separately, f_I(n) = f_II(n) = 0 for every odd perfect square n whenever 4 divides m, generalising a theorem of Elsholtz and Tao. Finally we prove the sharp local inequality 2B(n) >= A(n) for e_n in {1,3,5}, with a construction showing it fails for every odd e with 7 <= e <= 2*10^4; we conjecture f_I(p) > f_II(p) for all p > 5 with p not congruent to 1 mod 8, verify this for p <= 10^6, and reduce it to a finite window. We also locate exactly the factor log log N in the Elsholtz-Tao upper bound for the sum of f_I(p).
tags: Type I and Type II solutions
tldr: This paper studies the number of Type I and Type II solutions to the Erdős–Straus equation, establishing counting identities, concentration bounds, and local obstruction criteria.
motivation: The Erdős–Straus conjecture concerns whether 4/p can always be expressed as a sum of three unit fractions; this work shifts focus to counting the number of solutions and understanding their arithmetic structure.
method: The author uses a bijection of Bradford to derive exact counting identities involving divisor sums modulo e_n = 4n - p, and employs real Dirichlet characters to separate Type I and Type II solutions, with uniform and average-case bounds.
result: Type II solutions concentrate at x/p → 1/m, while Type I solutions cannot; f_I(n) = f_II(n) = 0 for odd perfect squares when 4 | m; a sharp local inequality 2B(n) ≥ A(n) holds for e_n ∈ {1,3,5} but fails for odd e between 7 and 2×10^4; the conjecture f_I(p) > f_II(p) is verified for p ≤ 10^6.
conclusion: The paper provides new arithmetic insights into solution counts of the Erdős–Straus equation, including concentration phenomena and local obstructions, but does not address the original conjecture.
keywords: Type I and Type II solutions

title: Support Discovery With Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares For Fixed-Charge Network Flow
authors: Christian K\"ummerle Sindura Saraswathi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fixed-charge network flow problem (FCNFP) couples continuous flow allocation with discrete arc-activation decisions, making it a canonical but computationally challenging model for a variety of network design and resource allocation problems. Exact mixed-integer linear programming formulations capture the fixed-charge structure faithfully, but often become difficult to solve on large networks. We propose a scalable continuous-optimization algorithm for large-scale single-commodity FCNFP based on an iteratively reweighted least-squares (IRLS) framework. The method replaces the discontinuous fixed-charge and linear arc cost objective with a smooth nonconvex Lasry--Lions surrogate and solves a sequence of weighted quadratic flow subproblems. Each subproblem is solved by a warm-started dual semismooth Newton method whose Newton systems have weighted graph-Laplacian structure, enabling the use of modern Laplacian solvers. To further improve the discovered arc supports of the challenging underlying combinatorial problem, we also develop an algorithmic variant that incorporates objective-driven perturbation restarts and an anchor-union restricted search that jointly leverages supports discovered by IRLS and by complementary FCNFP heuristics. Computational experiments on 410 benchmark, synthetic, and large-scale instances show that our method obtains the best objective quality among the evaluated scalable FCNFP algorithms, with a mean gap of [MATH] to a time-limited MILP reference and a win-or-tie rate of [MATH] among the non-MILP methods. The results indicate that combining smooth continuous optimization with support-level search is an effective strategy for producing high-quality feasible solutions to large-scale FCNFP.
tldr: The paper proposes an iteratively reweighted least-squares algorithm for large-scale fixed-charge network flow problems.
motivation: Fixed-charge network flow is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, and exact MILP methods struggle on large networks.
method: It uses a smooth nonconvex Lasry--Lions surrogate and solves weighted quadratic flow subproblems via a dual semismooth Newton method with graph-Laplacian structure, plus perturbation restarts and anchor-union restricted search.
result: Computational experiments on 410 instances show the method achieves the best objective quality among evaluated scalable FCNFP algorithms, with a mean gap to a time-limited MILP reference and a high win-or-tie rate.
conclusion: Combining smooth continuous optimization with support-level search is effective for producing high-quality feasible solutions to large-scale FCNFP.

title: Communication-efficient Admm Over Hierarchical Networks
authors: Binh Nguyen, Shuangqing Wei, Truong X. Nghiem
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a novel distributed optimization algorithm based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to solve hierarchical optimization problems over tree-structured networks, termed hierarchical ADMM (hADMM), with a particular focus on enhancing communication efficiency across the network. By rearranging the augmented Lagrangian to establish a query-response communication mechanism between nodes that explicitly exploits the hierarchical tree structure, the proposed algorithm significantly reduces communication costs compared to existing ADMM-based methods for hierarchical optimization. Furthermore, hADMM guarantees asymptotic convergence under convexity assumptions. We also present a convergence rate analysis based on linear matrix inequalities to characterize the maximum theoretically achievable convergence rates across different network topologies, showing that the proposed hADMM attains linear convergence under mild conditions. Three numerical experiments demonstrate that hADMM is compatible with arbitrary tree network structures and outperforms existing approaches in terms of communication efficiency.
tldr: The paper introduces hierarchical ADMM (hADMM), a distributed optimization algorithm for tree-structured networks that reduces communication cost while guaranteeing asymptotic convergence and linear convergence rates.
motivation: Existing ADMM-based methods for hierarchical optimization incur high communication overhead across network nodes, and there is a need for more communication-efficient algorithms that exploit the underlying tree topology.
method: The authors rearrange the augmented Lagrangian to create a query-response communication mechanism between nodes that explicitly uses the hierarchical tree structure, and they analyze convergence using linear matrix inequalities to bound achievable convergence rates.
result: hADMM significantly reduces communication cost compared to existing ADMM-based hierarchical methods, achieves linear convergence under mild convexity conditions, and is validated through three numerical experiments across arbitrary tree topologies.
conclusion: The proposed hADMM is compatible with arbitrary tree networks and outperforms existing approaches in communication efficiency, making it suitable for distributed optimization over hierarchical networks.

title: Finite Configurations Cannot Generate A Constant Trace In Rule 30
authors: David L. Condrey
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every right half we determine the unique left half whose Rule 30 central trace is constant: an alternating tail selected by the leading one of the right half when the initial center is 0, and a single universal checkerboard when it is 1. Every nonzero member of either fiber carries infinitely many ones, so the zero row is the only finite configuration with a constant trace. For support radius w the sharp maximum constant-prefix length is 2*ceil(w/2)+1 when the initial center is 0 and 2*floor(w/2)+2 when it is 1, so the maximum over both is w+2, attained by exactly 2^w configurations for even w and 2^w - 1 for odd w. Hence no column of a nonzero finite Rule 30 orbit is eventually constant.
tldr: The paper classifies finite configurations of Rule 30 whose central column trace is constant, showing only the all-zero configuration achieves this.
motivation: Rule 30 is a well-known elementary cellular automaton whose central column is used as a pseudorandom sequence, so understanding which finite initial conditions can produce constant traces is of foundational interest.
method: The author analyzes fibers over right halves to determine the unique compatible left half, characterizing them as alternating tails or a universal checkerboard depending on the initial center bit.
result: Every nonzero configuration in either fiber has infinitely many ones, and the maximum constant-prefix length for support radius w is w+2, attained by exactly 2^w configurations for even w and 2^w - 1 for odd w.
conclusion: No nonzero finite Rule 30 orbit can have an eventually constant column, confirming the necessity of infinite support for constant traces.

title: Unifying Variational View Of Accelerated Primal-Dual Methods
authors: Mehran Mesbahi Cheng Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unifying variational framework for accelerated primal-dual flows in affinely constrained convex optimization. In particular, it is shown that applying the Euler-Lagrange-Rayleigh (ELR) principle to coupled augmented Bregman Lagrangians systematically generates accelerated dynamics over general Bregman geometries and recovers a family of existing primal-dual mirror and Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) flows as special cases. We then establish [MATH] convergence guarantees for these flows under mild assumptions. Lastly, we show that the proposed framework for algorithmic development extends from finite-dimensional optimization to constrained optimization over probability distributions.
tldr: Develops a variational Euler-Lagrange-Rayleigh framework for accelerated primal-dual flows in affinely constrained convex optimization.
motivation: To unify and derive accelerated primal-dual methods such as mirror and ADMM flows from a single variational principle over general Bregman geometries.
method: Applies the Euler-Lagrange-Rayleigh principle to coupled augmented Bregman Lagrangians and establishes convergence guarantees for the resulting accelerated dynamics.
result: Recovers a family of existing primal-dual mirror and ADMM flows as special cases and extends the framework from finite-dimensional optimization to constrained optimization over probability distributions.
conclusion: The work provides a general variational template for accelerated algorithm design in convex optimization, but it is not related to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Stress-Based Estimator For Pressure And Stress Recovery From Velocity Measurements
authors: Nicol\'as Barnafi, Benjam\'in Cisternas, Ernesto Castillo, Felipe Galarce
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-invasive pressure field estimation from velocity measurements is a longstanding engineering problem. We propose, analyze, and test a pressure-recovery method that computes a full stress field from velocity measurements, and leaves the pressure estimation as a cheap post-processing step. The method relies on a stress-velocity first order formulation of the Navier-Stokes equations, and we show that the formulation accounts for deviations from incompressibility in the measured velocity field by construction. In addition, we theoretically establish the convergence of the finite element (FE) approximation scheme, the stability of the stress recovery with respect to finite-resolution velocity measurements, and then validate this theory numerically. Our results show that the proposed estimator is robust in convective flow regimes and remains accurate at reduced spatial resolution, improving upon state-of-the-art pressure-recovery strategies.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes a stress-based finite element estimator for recovering pressure and stress fields from velocity measurements in Navier-Stokes flows.
motivation: Non-invasive estimation of pressure fields from velocity data is a longstanding engineering problem, and existing pressure-recovery strategies struggle with convective regimes and reduced spatial resolution.
method: The authors use a stress-velocity first-order formulation of the Navier-Stokes equations, compute a full stress field from velocity measurements, and recover pressure as a cheap post-processing step, with finite element convergence and stability analysis.
result: Theoretical convergence and stability of the estimator with respect to finite-resolution velocity measurements are established and validated numerically, showing robustness in convective regimes and accuracy at reduced spatial resolution.
conclusion: The proposed stress-based estimator improves upon state-of-the-art pressure-recovery strategies and is robust to measurement resolution limits.

title: A Categorical Approach To Euclidean Ratios And Proportions
authors: Matthew Petersen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A categorial approach to the non-metric geometry in Books V and VI of Euclid's is presented. Specifically, we introduce a diagrammatic syntax that can be overlaid immediately on his diagrams, thus bridging intuitive presentation with fidelity to Euclid's arguments. This syntax makes complicated definitions like V.5, and indeed the arguments throughout books V and VI, including arguments about similar figures, intuitively clear. We show in an appendix that this syntax can be used to solve a puzzle regarding ancient mathematics. Finally, we offer evidence that this approach to Euclidean diagrams is rooted in the Aristotelian tradition itself, and that a similar syntax was utilized, in antiquity, for related questions of numeric and proportions. Thus the syntax is plausibly faithful to Euclid's own thought-world, and not an outside-imposition.
tldr: The paper introduces a diagrammatic categorical syntax for Euclidean ratios and proportions in Books V and VI, arguing it aligns with Aristotelian and ancient mathematical traditions.
motivation: The author aims to bridge intuitive geometric presentation with fidelity to Euclid's arguments and to solve a puzzle in ancient mathematics.
method: A categorical/diagrammatic syntax is overlaid on Euclidean diagrams, with an appendix applying it to an ancient mathematical puzzle and comparative evidence from Aristotelian and ancient numeric/proportional practices.
result: The syntax clarifies complicated definitions such as Euclid V.5 and arguments about similar figures, and is argued to be plausibly faithful to Euclid's own thought-world.
conclusion: The approach offers a historically grounded reinterpretation of Euclidean proportion theory, but it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Central Limit Theorems And Bootstrap For Sparse Regularized Multimarginal Optimal Transport And Barycenters
authors: Pengtao Li, Alberto Gonz\'alez-Sanz, Xiaohui Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wasserstein barycenters are a fundamental tool for the analysis of distribution-valued data, but their computation and statistical analysis become challenging in high-dimensional and multi-sample settings. The unregularized barycenter problem is computationally demanding and suffers severely from the curse of dimensionality, making regularization essential in many applications. While regularized optimal transport methods are widely used, approaches based on entropic penalization tend to overspread mass and may blur the geometric structure of the solution. Motivated by barycenter estimation, we propose a more general methodology based on sparse regularized multimarginal optimal transport (RMOT). Our formulation creates sparse transport plans and is designed to avoid this overspreading effect. We establish consistency, central limit theorems, and bootstrap validity for the optimal potentials and couplings for the empirical RMOT problem. Specializing to sparse regularized barycenters, our results yield a uniform weak limit and bootstrap consistency. Numerical simulations show that sparsity plays a fundamental role in preserving the structure of the solution and avoiding the overspreading behavior typical of entropic regularization.
tldr: The paper develops central limit theorems and bootstrap validity for sparse regularized multimarginal optimal transport and Wasserstein barycenters.
motivation: Wasserstein barycenters are useful for distribution-valued data but suffer from computational and statistical challenges in high dimensions; entropic regularization overspreads mass and blurs geometric structure.
method: The authors propose sparse regularized multimarginal optimal transport (RMOT) to obtain sparse transport plans and avoid overspreading, then establish consistency, central limit theorems, and bootstrap validity for optimal potentials and couplings.
result: They prove uniform weak limits and bootstrap consistency for sparse regularized barycenters, and numerical simulations show sparsity preserves solution structure and mitigates overspreading.
conclusion: Sparse regularization provides a statistically principled and computationally practical alternative to entropic regularization for multimarginal optimal transport and barycenter estimation.

title: A Function-Space Framework For Bddc Preconditioning In Control- And State-Constrained Sparse Optimal Control
authors: Harbir Antil, Keegan L. A. Kirk, Umarkhon Rakhimov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) preconditioner for the interface systems arising from active-set semi-smooth Newton linearizations of elliptic optimal control problems with box-constrained controls, [MATH]-sparsity, and Moreau--Yosida regularized state constraints. The domain decomposition and BDDC construction are formulated directly at the infinite-dimensional level. Eliminating the interior variables yields a Schur complement for the state and adjoint traces assembled from local subdomain operators. We prove a global--local equivalence result, establish well-posedness of the local and partially assembled problems under verifiable conditions on the primal constraints. The BDDC operator admits a two-level additive Schwarz representation with independent local solves and a finite-dimensional coarse solve. We implement the preconditioner using conforming finite elements and test it for distributed and Neumann boundary control. For a fixed ratio of subdomain diameter [MATH] to mesh size [MATH], the GMRES iteration counts are nearly independent of mesh refinement and grow only moderately as this ratio increases. Enriching the coarse space substantially improves convergence and reduces sensitivity to the control regularization and sparsity weights. For the state-constrained problem, scaling the Moreau--Yosida penalty parameter proportionally to [MATH] yields nearly constant GMRES iteration counts as the mesh is refined.
tldr: The paper develops an infinite-dimensional BDDC domain decomposition preconditioner for interface systems arising from active-set semi-smooth Newton linearizations of elliptic optimal control problems with box-constrained controls, sparsity, and Moreau–Yosida regularized state constraints.
motivation: Solving large-scale sparse optimal control problems with control and state constraints requires efficient, scalable solvers whose convergence is robust under mesh refinement and parameter changes.
method: The BDDC construction is formulated at the infinite-dimensional level, eliminating interior variables to obtain a Schur complement for state and adjoint traces; a global–local equivalence result and well-posedness of local and partially assembled problems are proven, yielding a two-level additive Schwarz representation implemented with conforming finite elements.
result: For fixed subdomain-to-mesh-size ratio, GMRES iteration counts are nearly mesh-independent and grow only moderately with the ratio; enriching the coarse space improves convergence, and scaling the Moreau–Yosida penalty proportionally to the mesh size keeps iteration counts nearly constant.
conclusion: The function-space BDDC framework provides a scalable, parameter-robust preconditioner for constrained elliptic optimal control, though it lies entirely outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Characterizing Multi-Cell Pinching-Antenna Transmission: Revealing The Other Side Of The Coin
authors: Zhiguo Ding
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using pinching antennas to enhance a user's connection to its own base station (BS) is intuitive and has been well investigated in the literature. This letter focuses on a less intuitive advantage of pinching antennas from the interference-suppression perspective. In particular, using pinching antennas ensures that all BSs serve their users with low transmit power, i.e., BSs can ``whisper", rather than ``shout", to their users. As a result, by experiencing less interference, a user's data rate can still be improved with pinching antennas, even if its link quality to its own BS remains unchanged. A stochastic geometric study is carried out in the letter, where BSs employ fractional power control. Analytical and numerical results are presented to reveal the significant impact of this interference-suppression capability offered by pinching antennas.
tldr: This letter analyzes multi-cell pinching-antenna transmission and shows that pinching antennas can suppress interference by allowing base stations to transmit with lower power, improving user data rates even without link-quality gains.
motivation: Pinching antennas are typically studied for enhancing a user's connection to its own base station, but the paper explores the less intuitive advantage of interference suppression in multi-cell networks.
method: A stochastic geometric study is carried out for base stations employing fractional power control, with analytical and numerical results comparing pinching-antenna and conventional transmission.
result: The analysis reveals that pinching antennas enable base stations to 'whisper' rather than 'shout', reducing interference so that a user's data rate can improve even if its own link quality remains unchanged.
conclusion: The interference-suppression capability of pinching antennas provides a significant multi-cell performance benefit, highlighting a complementary advantage beyond link enhancement.

title: Signal Correlation, Ic, And PnL Dependence
authors: Marc Nunes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Signal correlation and PnL correlation are correlations over different index sets - across assets at each date versus across dates for scalar payoffs - and practitioners often treat the first as a proxy for the second. We give an exact decomposition that shows what that proxy sees and what it discards. We recall that at each date a normalized signal's projection onto the realized demeaned return direction is its realized cross-sectional Pearson IC, so that fixed-signal PnL is return dispersion times IC (Qian and Hua, 2004), and we identify the normalized similarity of two signals in the orthogonal complement as their partial correlation controlling for realized returns; the residual rotational freedom is an orthogonal gauge whose invariants are the transverse Gram matrix. Signal correlation therefore equals an uncentered IC cross-moment plus transverse similarity, while Pearson PnL correlation centers and dispersion-weights the IC series alone. Our main result is a non-identifiability theorem: absent constraints on transverse geometry, neither correlation bounds or orders the other, which sharpens the simulation finding of Sorensen, Qian, Schoen, and Hua (2004) into an exact statement. For normalized ensembles the transverse Gram matrix re-enters through the normalization denominator; the ex post optimal combination under Euclidean and general covariance-risk metrics is the classical multiple-correlation bound, and we show that the two rules agree for every longitudinal exposure if and only if the risk metric is isotropic on the signal span. The classical exact null law of partial correlation under isotropy, a synthetic mechanism illustration at weak-IC scales, and inference guidance under temporal dependence complete the treatment.
tldr: A quantitative-finance paper decomposing the relationship between signal correlation and PnL correlation via an orthogonal-gauge framework, proving a non-identifiability theorem between the two.
motivation: Practitioners often treat cross-sectional signal correlation as a proxy for PnL correlation, and the authors aim to clarify exactly what this proxy captures and what it discards.
method: The paper gives an exact decomposition of normalized signals into a component along realized demeaned returns (the realized Pearson IC) plus a transverse complement, using Gram-matrix invariants and gauge-theoretic reasoning.
result: A non-identifiability theorem shows that, absent constraints on transverse geometry, signal correlation and PnL correlation neither bound nor order one another, sharpening earlier simulation findings into an exact statement.
conclusion: The work provides inference guidance and exact null laws for partial correlation under isotropy, clarifying when the two correlation notions can be compared.

title: Counterexamples For BFGS-type Methods Under Arbitrary Strong Wolfe Constants
authors: Rui Diao
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) method and its variants can fail to converge on smooth nonconvex functions under realistic line-search parameters has remained a central open problem in quasi-Newton theory since the landmark counterexample of Dai (2002), which was confined to small Armijo parameters ([MATH] on Powell's geometry, or [MATH] on his six-point cycle) and an objective function unbounded below. In this paper, we resolve the long-standing open question, posed by Dai (2002) following a discussion with J. C. Gilbert, of whether such counterexamples exist in theory for every Armijo parameter [MATH]. Specifically, for every prescribed pair of line-search parameters [MATH], we construct an objective function [MATH], bounded below and with Lipschitz continuous gradient, on which every method in a broad conjugacy class [MATH] equipped with the first-local-minimizer line search generates an infinite sequence of iterates with [MATH] for all [MATH]. The class [MATH] encompasses the classical full-memory BFGS method, limited-memory BFGS (L-BFGS) with arbitrary memory [MATH], the Broyden positive family, and the Hestenes-Stiefel conjugate gradient method. The steps are the standard first local minimizers along the search rays and simultaneously satisfy the strong Wolfe, weak Wolfe, Armijo, and Goldstein conditions with constants [MATH]. The construction operates in the minimal possible dimension [MATH], exploiting a non-decaying conjugate descent orbit in the plane coupled with an explicit tubular interpolation whose two-bump axial curvature profile places the Armijo ratio anywhere in [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs counterexamples showing that BFGS-type quasi-Newton methods can fail to converge for arbitrary strong Wolfe line-search constants, resolving an open problem posed by Dai (2002).
motivation: Whether BFGS and its variants can diverge on smooth nonconvex objectives under realistic line-search parameters had been open since Dai's limited counterexample, which only worked for small Armijo parameters and unbounded-below functions.
method: For every prescribed pair of line-search parameters, the authors build a bounded-below objective with Lipschitz gradient in two dimensions, using a non-decaying conjugate descent orbit and an explicit tubular interpolation with a two-bump axial curvature profile.
result: Every method in a broad conjugacy class (full-memory BFGS, L-BFGS with arbitrary memory, Broyden positive family, Hestenes-Stiefel CG) equipped with the first-local-minimizer line search produces an infinite iterate sequence failing to converge, while satisfying strong Wolfe, weak Wolfe, Armijo and Goldstein conditions.
conclusion: The results definitively answer the long-standing question of whether BFGS-type counterexamples exist for all admissible line-search constants, in the minimal possible dimension.

title: Closed-loop $\alpha$-Potential Stochastic Differential Games Via A Bsde Approach
authors: Liangquan Zhang Xun Li
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the closed-loop [MATH]-potential stochastic differential game (SDG) problem as a continuation of our prior research on open-loop control (see ). By utilizing the backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) approach, we derive a precise estimate for the parameter [MATH]. Compared to our earlier work , this study incorporates both first- and second-order sensitivity state processes, as well as the sensitivity of the control process. A distinguishing feature of this work is that, in the context of [MATH]-player heterogeneous agent games involving mean-field type interactions, we derive an [MATH]-uniform upper bound for the minimal potential approximation error. In contrast to the corresponding open-loop estimates, the closed-loop bound contains feedback-induced contributions that need not vanish with [MATH]. Consequently, our present estimate does not in general guarantee [MATH].
tldr: The paper studies closed-loop α-potential stochastic differential games using a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) approach, deriving uniform bounds on approximation error for mean-field heterogeneous agent games.
motivation: This work extends prior open-loop control research to closed-loop α-potential games and seeks precise estimates for the parameter α while incorporating sensitivity of state and control processes.
method: The authors employ the BSDE approach, including first- and second-order sensitivity processes for both state and control, to analyze N-player heterogeneous mean-field games.
result: They obtain an N-uniform upper bound for the minimal potential approximation error, showing that closed-loop bounds contain feedback-induced contributions that need not vanish as N grows, so the earlier estimate does not generally guarantee a vanishing bound.
conclusion: The closed-loop formulation introduces persistent feedback effects that distinguish it from open-loop settings, and the derived bound highlights limitations of the α-potential approximation in heterogeneous mean-field games.

title: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks On Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
authors: Zhihao Liu, Hongyu Sun, Zhiyuan Fu, Xiaonan Duan, Jice Wang, Shangru Zhao, Weizhi Meng, Wuxin Yang, Yangfan Zhou, Yuqing Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end evaluation framework for image-triggered command injection against computer-use agents (CUAs). The goal is to test whether a local visual patch can induce verifiable environmental consequences along the full chain of screenshot input, VLM generation, action parsing, and environment execution. We train and deploy patches on author-controlled GitHub Pages pages and a locally deployed CSDN clone, and evaluate them in real environments across five open-source or publicly available GUI-agent or vision-language-model (VLM) backends. Our experiment aggregates 600 instance-level online cases, with T-ASR, TAPR, and E2E-ASR reaching 84.5%, 47.0%, and 20.3%, respectively. Trajectory analysis further shows that in some successful cases the agent first executes a malicious terminal command and then continues the original benign task. These results indicate that optimized local visual signals can affect not only VLM outputs but also propagate through the execution pipeline of open CUAs and create real environmental risk.
tldr: The paper evaluates whether locally optimized visual adversarial patches can hijack multimodal computer-use agents into executing attacker-chosen commands in real GUI environments.
motivation: Computer-use agents driven by vision-language models are increasingly deployed to operate real software, creating a new attack surface where visual input can be manipulated to trigger unintended actions.
method: The authors train and deploy adversarial visual patches on author-controlled GitHub Pages and a local CSDN clone, then test them end-to-end across five open-source GUI-agent and VLM backends, scoring success via T-ASR, TAPR, and E2E-ASR over 600 online cases.
result: T-ASR, TAPR, and E2E-ASR reach 84.5%, 47.0%, and 20.3% respectively, with trajectory analysis showing some agents execute malicious terminal commands before resuming their benign task.
conclusion: Optimized local visual signals can propagate through the full screenshot-to-execution pipeline of open computer-use agents, producing verifiable real-world environmental risk.

title: In Rag We Trust? Measuring Robustness Of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Under Document Poisoning
authors: Iliano Fasolino
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds a language model in retrieved documents, which reduces hallucination but creates a new attack surface: if retrieved text is tampered with, the model may repeat the falsehood. We study how much a small quantized model, Llama 3.1 8B, degrades when a fraction of its retrieved context is poisoned. Three corruption strategies are tested, entity swap, number swap, and negation, each applied to zero, one, two, or three of the three retrieved passages, over a factorial sweep of 588 runs on a fact-checking task built from FEVER. Accuracy falls from 77.9% on clean context to 43.5% when all three passages are corrupted. Entity swap flips the largest share of answers that were correct on clean context. Number-based corruption stays flat while poisoned passages are a minority and jumps once they form a majority, a pattern we re-check with query-level bootstrap intervals. The model rarely invents new falsehoods; its dominant reaction is to abstain, and a lexical overlap proxy of unsupported generation falls under attack rather than rising. The study is a small-scale measurement with coarse automated labels; we treat the strategy contrasts as suggestive until decoding is controlled and stronger adjudication is in place.
tldr: A small-scale empirical study measuring how much a quantized Llama 3.1 8B degrades on a FEVER-based fact-checking task when retrieved RAG passages are deliberately poisoned.
motivation: RAG reduces hallucination by grounding generation in retrieved documents, but this creates an attack surface where tampered retrieved text can propagate falsehoods; the extent of degradation under partial poisoning is unclear.
method: Three corruption strategies (entity swap, number swap, negation) were applied to 0, 1, 2, or 3 of three retrieved passages across a factorial sweep of 588 runs, with query-level bootstrap intervals for the number-swap pattern.
result: Accuracy dropped from 77.9% on clean context to 43.5% when all three passages were corrupted; entity swap flipped the most clean-correct answers, number corruption stayed flat under minority poisoning and jumped once poisoned passages became a majority, and the model mostly abstained rather than inventing new falsehoods.
conclusion: The authors frame this as a coarse, small-scale measurement whose strategy contrasts remain suggestive until decoding is controlled and stronger adjudication is used.

title: X-amine509: Predicting The Practical Risk Level Of Enterprise X.509 Certificates
authors: Cameron Keith, Shubh Patel, JD Kilgallin, Caleb Shorter
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprises managing large X.509 certificate inventories face a prioritization problem: deterministic analysis tools that precisely identify standards violations are indispensable for remediation, but applying them exhaustively across millions of certificates is operationally impractical. We present X-amine509, a two-stage triage system that uses machine learning to rapidly rank certificates by predicted risk and route only the highest-risk items to full deterministic analysis. Certificate risk is quantified as a composite score derived from 177 defect checks grounded in CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, NIST IR 8547/SP 800-57, and cryptographic strength criteria, weighted by security severity across four tiers ranging from cryptographic breaks to minor compliance deviations. We collected 1,027,714 X.509 certificates from Fortune 500, .gov, and .edu domains and scored each using this rubric. On a held-out test set of 201,976 certificates, our best model (Extra Trees) achieves [MATH] of 0.993 with MAE of 2.26, while Decision Tree scores [MATH] of 0.986 at 3.7 million certificates per second on a single machine. Ranking quality confirms the triage value: aggregate NDCG exceeds 0.997, and severity-tier classification reports 99.76% accuracy with 98.90% recall on critical-tier defects. Thirteen months later, we retrieved another 571,374 certificates to test our models' durability over time, and the Extra Trees and Decision Tree models maintain MAE below 6.8, [MATH] of at least 0.915, aggregate NDCG above 0.988, severity-tier accuracy of at least 99.52%, and critical-tier recall of at least 97.03%. Feature importance analysis identifies validity period, Extended Key Usage configuration, negative serial number encoding, and self-signed status as the strongest risk predictors, providing coarse interpretability at the triage stage.
tldr: X-amine509 is a two-stage machine learning triage system that ranks enterprise X.509 certificates by predicted risk to prioritize full deterministic analysis.
motivation: Enterprises managing millions of X.509 certificates cannot exhaustively apply standards-based deterministic checks, creating a need for scalable risk prioritization.
method: The authors collected over 1 million certificates, scored them using a composite risk rubric based on 177 defect checks from CA/Browser Forum and NIST standards, and trained models including Extra Trees and Decision Tree.
result: The best model achieves R² of 0.993 with MAE 2.26 on a held-out test set, with high NDCG and severity-tier accuracy; performance remains strong after thirteen months.
conclusion: Machine learning can effectively and durably triage certificate risk, enabling practical prioritization of X.509 remediation while preserving interpretability via feature importance.

title: An Experimental Evaluation Of Multimodal Prompt Injection Attacks On Agentic Ai Frameworks
authors: Mohammad I. Husain Viet K. Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI frameworks let a language model plan, keep memory, and call tools that reach real files, mail, and services. Most of these agents also read images, which gives an attacker a way to put text into the agent's context without going through the user. We present MMPIBench, a reproducible benchmark that measures what happens next. It delivers a fixed set of attacks through six visual carriers (OCR text, overlays, EXIF metadata, QR codes, fake interfaces, and hybrids) and records how far each injected instruction travels through the agent, from perception through planning to the tool call. Across 720 runs covering six frameworks, five foundation models, six carriers, and four attacker objectives, attacks complete in approximately 1% of runs but are attempted in 12.8%, and the gap is closed almost entirely at the planning step, where the model reads the injected instruction and declines to act on it. The model matters far more than the framework for whether an instruction is acted on. One model never attempts an attack and recognizes the injection in 59.7% of runs, while two others attempt in 23.6%. We then extend the benchmark to audio, the only other raw perceptual channel current frontier models accept. Only two of the five models ingest audio and only three of the six frameworks deliver it, but where the signal arrives the attack completes in 49% of cells, and in 75% for one model. Reporting completion alone therefore understates exposure, and perceptual channels beyond vision are narrower but much less defended.
tldr: MMPIBench is a reproducible benchmark measuring multimodal prompt injection attacks across agentic AI frameworks via visual and audio carriers.
motivation: Agentic AI systems that read images or audio can receive adversarial instructions through perceptual channels without user mediation, creating an understudied security exposure.
method: The benchmark delivers fixed attacks through visual carriers (OCR text, overlays, EXIF metadata, QR codes, fake interfaces, hybrids) across six frameworks and five foundation models, tracking instruction propagation from perception to planning to tool calls, then extends testing to audio.
result: Visual attacks complete in about 1% of runs but are attempted in 12.8%, with the planning step blocking most attempts; audio attacks complete in 49% of delivered cases and 75% for one model.
conclusion: Completion rates understate exposure, and non-visual perceptual channels are narrower but much less defended than vision in current agentic AI frameworks.

title: DuplexJail: Safety Alignment Breaks Under Spoken Interruption In Full-Duplex Models
authors: Jaechul Roh, Deepak Chandran, Amir Houmansadr, Andrea Fanelli
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-duplex speech models accept user speech while generating responses, creating an underexplored attack surface. We introduce DuplexJail, which delivers fixed, request-independent spoken prompts through the user audio channel. We compare fixed-delay interruption after the harmful request ends with refusal-triggered interruption following a cue in the model's streaming text. Across four open-source models and 720 harmful requests from AdvBench and HarmBench, fixed-delay interruption raises whole-response attack success rates on AdvBench to 40.3% for PersonaPlex and 48.7% for PersonaPlex-RL, increases of +33.8 and +39.3 percentage points. The refusal-triggered policy reaches 35.6% and 48.6%, respectively, with all trials scored regardless of whether an interruption occurs. Selected conditions also increase FLM-Audio's harmful-response rate, while BayLing-Duplex shows decreases. These findings identify spoken interruption as a jailbreak attack vector and motivate evaluating safety throughout ongoing full-duplex interaction.
tldr: DuplexJail demonstrates that spoken interruptions delivered through the user audio channel can jailbreak full-duplex speech models, substantially raising attack success rates on harmful requests.
motivation: Full-duplex speech models accept user speech while generating responses, creating an underexplored attack surface for safety alignment failures that prior text-based jailbreak research has not addressed.
method: The authors introduce fixed, request-independent spoken prompts inserted via two interruption policies (fixed-delay after the harmful request, and refusal-triggered following a cue in the model's streaming text), tested across four open-source full-duplex models and 720 harmful requests from AdvBench and HarmBench.
result: Fixed-delay interruption raised whole-response attack success rates to 40.3% for PersonaPlex and 48.7% for PersonaPlex-RL (increases of +33.8 and +39.3 percentage points), with the refusal-triggered policy reaching 35.6% and 48.6%; effects varied across models, including decreases for BayLing-Duplex.
conclusion: Spoken interruption is identified as a novel jailbreak vector, motivating safety evaluation and mitigation throughout ongoing full-duplex interaction rather than only at response boundaries.

title: Fast Constraint Extraction For Corrective Control Under Stl Specifications Via Logical Dependency Tracking
authors: Antoine Besset, Joris Tillet, Chuchu Fan, Julien Alexandre Dit Sandretto
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensuring the satisfaction of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications under uncertainty is challenging, as reachability-based monitoring provides guarantees but does not indicate how to restore satisfaction when it becomes indeterminate. A key difficulty is identifying which uncertain components actually affect global satisfaction, especially for nested formulas. This paper introduces a logical dependency tracking framework that propagates uncertainty through the STL structure and captures the causal contribution of reachable sets to satisfaction. By associating markers to uncertain predicates and propagating them via three-valued semantics, we extract in milliseconds a compact Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF) of sufficient constraints, avoiding combinatorial enumeration. As an application, we formulate control correction as a minimum-effort optimization problem. Using zonotopic reachability, the derived constraints are enforced via linear programming, yielding corrections that guarantee STL satisfaction under bounded uncertainty and provide certified probabilistic bounds in the stochastic case. We demonstrate the approach on a nonlinear system with nested STL specifications, showing that dependency tracking enables efficient and formally guaranteed correction. The tracking implementation is available at [URL].
tldr: The paper presents a logical dependency tracking framework that extracts compact sufficient constraints from Signal Temporal Logic (STL) specifications to enable fast corrective control under uncertainty.
motivation: Reachability-based STL monitoring can guarantee satisfaction but offers no guidance on how to restore satisfaction when it becomes indeterminate, and identifying which uncertain components affect nested formulas is combinatorially hard.
method: Markers are attached to uncertain predicates and propagated through the STL structure using three-valued semantics, yielding a compact DNF of sufficient constraints in milliseconds; control correction is then cast as a minimum-effort optimization solved via linear programming over zonotopic reachable sets.
result: On a nonlinear system with nested STL specifications, the approach produces formally guaranteed corrections under bounded uncertainty and certified probabilistic bounds in the stochastic case, avoiding combinatorial enumeration.
conclusion: Dependency tracking enables efficient, formally verified corrective control for STL specifications, though the work is entirely within formal methods and control theory with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: An Efficient And Effective Agentic Group Shilling Attack On Recommender Systems
authors: Quoc Viet Nguyen, Trinh Pham, Viet Huynh, Hongzhi Yin, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Bay Vo, Thanh Tam Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recommender systems have become core infrastructure for modern online platforms, personalizing content at scale and strongly influencing what users see, click on, and purchase. However, this dependence on user interaction also exposes them to shilling attacks, where malicious actors can inject fake profiles to distort item rankings and control visibility. Existing attacks often rely on target-specific fine-tuning or fixed profile templates, making them either difficult to adapt to different victims or easier to detect. To overcome these limitations, we propose the Agentic Group Attack System (AGAS), a coordinated shilling framework where a central Coordinator directs a group of role-switching worker agents to adaptively promote a target item across different victim families. The Coordinator dynamically adjusts the strategy when progress stalls or suppression signals increase, while workers pursue a shared objective and switch between active and inactive roles to avoid repetitive patterns. Under the same attack budgets and evaluation protocols, AGAS consistently surpasses strong baselines in target promotion while better preserving benign recommendation quality, weakening representative detectors, and achieving higher efficiency than prior attacks. These findings also emphasize that defending recommender systems may require mechanisms that can handle adaptive shilling campaigns, not just isolated fake-profile injections. Our code is available at [URL].
tldr: The paper proposes AGAS, an agentic group-based shilling attack framework that uses a central coordinator and role-switching worker agents to adaptively promote target items in recommender systems.
motivation: Recommender systems are vulnerable to shilling attacks where fake profiles distort rankings, but existing attacks rely on target-specific fine-tuning or fixed templates, making them hard to adapt or easy to detect.
method: AGAS employs a central Coordinator that dynamically adjusts attack strategy in response to stalled progress or suppression signals, directing a group of role-switching worker agents that toggle between active and inactive roles to avoid repetitive patterns while sharing a common objective.
result: Under matched attack budgets and evaluation protocols, AGAS outperforms strong baselines in target promotion, better preserves benign recommendation quality, weakens representative detectors, and achieves higher efficiency than prior attacks.
conclusion: The findings suggest that defending recommender systems requires mechanisms capable of handling adaptive, coordinated shilling campaigns rather than isolated fake-profile injections.

title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment At Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack On A 320b MoE
authors: Yi Shi, Tanyu Chen, Kai Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directional ablation removes an aligned language model's ability to refuse by projecting a single "refusal direction" out of the weights that write the residual stream. It needs no gradient-based training and no optimization, only a few hundred contrastive prompts, which makes it the canonical white-box attack on open-weight alignment. However, it has been established only on dense models up to roughly 70B parameters. We study whether it survives the shift to frontier mixture-of-experts (MoE) models whose residual streams are no longer a single tensor and whose weights ship quantized. We apply it to GLM-5.3-Flash (320B parameters, 288 routed experts, a four-wide hyper-connection residual, block-FP8). The attack survives the architecture, but what it reaches is no longer where a reader of the original recipe would look for it. Editing the attention, dense and routed-expert writers on their own removes 0.039, 0.016 and 0.148 of refusal respectively; editing all three together removes 0.776. As a result, 74% of the effect exists only under the joint intervention. The part the conventional recipe reaches by module-name matching accounts for 0.066 of that 0.776, which is why it fails silently on an MoE. The effect does not follow from removing just any direction: ablating a random direction orthogonal to it leaves refusal unchanged. A category-concentrated residue survives every edit we tried: subspaces fitted on violence, sexual content and hate leave measurable refusal at every rank from 1 to 12. We report the method, the 41-89 percentage-point reductions it achieves across seven harmful benchmarks with no detected change in capability, and the boundary where it stops.
tldr: The paper studies whether directional ablation, a white-box attack that removes refusal behavior by projecting out a single direction in weight space, remains effective on a 320B-parameter mixture-of-experts frontier model.
motivation: Directional ablation is a canonical attack on open-weight alignment but had only been tested on dense models up to about 70B parameters, leaving unclear whether it survives frontier MoE architectures with quantized weights and non-single-tensor residual streams.
method: The authors apply directional ablation to GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-parameter MoE model with 288 routed experts, a four-wide hyper-connection residual, and block-FP8 quantization, testing separate and joint edits of attention, dense, and routed-expert writers.
result: The attack survives the architecture but requires joint intervention: editing attention, dense, and routed-expert writers removes 0.776 of refusal, with 74% of the effect only under joint editing, yielding 41-89 percentage-point reductions across seven harmful benchmarks without detected capability loss.
conclusion: Conventional module-name-matching recipes fail silently on MoE models because they target only a small fraction of the effect, and a category-concentrated residue remains that resists all tested edits.

title: CrossLink: Breaking Location Privacy By Linking Device Identifiers Across Protocols
authors: Aneet Kumar Dutta, Mihirraj Dixit, Kevin Gni, Wouter Lueks, Mridula Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Smartphones simultaneously transmit temporary identifiers over LTE, WiFi, and BLE. Existing privacy defenses analyze identifier randomization per protocol, implicitly assuming that these protections compose across protocols. We show that they do not: Even when each protocol leaks only temporary identifiers and the adversary is fully passive, unsynchronized identifier rotations allow cross-protocol stitching of device traces. We present CrossLink, an uncertainty-aware tracing algorithm that links identifiers across time, space, and protocols under noisy localization and mobility. We evaluate CrossLink using controlled lab experiments with commodity devices and large-scale mobility simulation. Under large-scale mobility simulation, CrossLink reconstructs full traces for 83% of users, versus 22% for the best single-protocol baseline, showing that location privacy must be analyzed jointly across protocols. We further show that CrossLink remains effective under partial coverage: strategically placed sniffers near LTE handover regions, mobile sniffers, and limited high-coverage subregions retain sufficient cross-protocol evidence to bridge observation gaps, achieving substantially higher linkability than random deployments.
tldr: CrossLink demonstrates that location privacy defenses fail when identifier randomization is analyzed separately across LTE, WiFi, and BLE, enabling cross-protocol device tracking.
motivation: Existing privacy protections assume identifier rotation composes across protocols, but unsynchronized rotations may allow passive adversaries to stitch together device traces.
method: The authors develop CrossLink, an uncertainty-aware tracing algorithm that links temporary identifiers across time, space, and protocols under noisy localization and mobility, evaluated via lab experiments and large-scale mobility simulation.
result: CrossLink reconstructs full traces for 83% of users under simulation, compared to 22% for the best single-protocol baseline, and remains effective under partial coverage with strategically placed sniffers.
conclusion: Location privacy must be analyzed jointly across protocols, as cross-protocol linking breaks per-protocol randomization defenses even for fully passive adversaries.

title: Policy Change For Treelike Monitors
authors: Fran\c{c}ois Hublet, Dhruv Nevatia, Joshua Schneider
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the policy change problem that arises in the runtime verification of long-running systems. The online monitors typically used in this context are generally treelike, in that they maintain substates that monitor subformulae of the target policy. We consider when and how the policy can be changed while the monitored system is running by only exploiting the information stored in the monitor's state. This is relevant, for example, to account for new system functionality or changes in regulatory requirements. We formally define the policy change problem in a general setting, independent of any specific (treelike) monitor implementation. We then show that policy change for past-time metric temporal logic (pMTL) is decidable but has tight non-primitive recursive lower and upper bounds, while with discrete-time semantics it is EXPSPACE-complete.
tldr: The paper formalizes the policy change problem for treelike runtime monitors and establishes decidability and complexity bounds for past-time metric temporal logic.
motivation: Long-running systems often need runtime verification policies updated while the system runs, but it is unclear when and how policies can be changed using only the monitor's stored state.
method: The authors define the policy change problem abstractly, independent of monitor implementation, and analyze it for past-time metric temporal logic under dense and discrete-time semantics.
result: Policy change for pMTL is decidable with tight non-primitive recursive bounds, and EXPSPACE-complete under discrete-time semantics.
conclusion: The work provides a formal foundation and complexity characterization for dynamically updating treelike runtime monitors, relevant to runtime verification rather than quantum information research.

title: Understanding The Security Boundary Of Obfuscation-based On-Device Llm Protection
authors: Hanyi Zhou, Chenyang Li, Yuanzhe Pang, Ke Xu, Mingwei Xu, Zhuotao Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) offer a promising mechanism for safeguarding the intellectual property of on-device Large Language Models (LLMs). To overcome the inherent computational bottlenecks of TEEs, existing TEE-Shielded LLM Partition (TSLP) methods apply efficient obfuscation schemes to computationally intensive layers, offloading them to external GPUs while retaining only lightweight operations within the TEE. Although a growing body of TSLP-based approaches has emerged, these defense mechanisms remain largely heuristic. Consequently, some methods are proven vulnerable to certain specialized adversarial attacks designed to exploit their specific architectural implementations. To overcome the limitations of these heuristic designs, this paper addresses a fundamental research question: can we establish common primitives to unify representative prior methodologies, characterize the security boundary of their compositions, and systematically extend them? To this end, we formalize a set of obfuscation primitives, defined as dual-tuples of linear computations satisfying specific algebraic properties. We demonstrate that the matrix-level weight transformations of the representative efficient TSLP frameworks studied in this paper can be expressed as compositions of these primitives; consequently, the canonical form of these primitive compositions, denoted as O_prior, characterizes the structural boundary of this primitive family. We then expose the vulnerabilities of O_prior through a novel primitive-guided attack methodology, Collapse, demonstrating a shared vulnerability in several prominent TSLP methods published in top-tier venues, such as ArrowCloak (Security'25), TSQP (S&P'25), and LoRO (NeurIPS'25). Finally, we introduce two novel obfuscation primitives and integrate them with existing constructs to formulate O_ext, extending this security boundary.
tldr: The paper formalizes obfuscation primitives to characterize the security boundary of TEE-shielded LLM partitioning and proposes new primitives to extend it.
motivation: TEEs are promising for protecting on-device LLM intellectual property, but computational bottlenecks require obfuscation-based offloading, and existing TEE-Shielded LLM Partition (TSLP) defenses are heuristic and vulnerable to specialized attacks.
method: The authors define obfuscation primitives as dual-tuples of linear computations, show that prior TSLP weight transformations can be expressed as compositions of these primitives, introduce a primitive-guided attack called Collapse, and propose two novel primitives to form an extended boundary O_ext.
result: The canonical form O_prior characterizes the structural boundary of the primitive family and exposes a shared vulnerability in prominent TSLP methods including ArrowCloak (Security'25), TSQP (S&P'25), and LoRO (NeurIPS'25); O_ext extends the security boundary with new primitives.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for understanding and systematically extending the security boundary of obfuscation-based on-device LLM protection, revealing fundamental limits of existing TSLP approaches.

title: On The Tightness Of Standard Relaxations For Mixed-Integer Bilevel Linear Programs
authors: Oleg A. Prokopyev Sergey S. Ketkov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.10233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact algorithms for solving mixed-integer bilevel linear programs (MIBLPs) typically rely on sequences of lower and upper bounds that converge to the optimal value. These procedures are commonly initialized using the single-level relaxation (SLR), obtained by omitting the follower's optimality condition and solving the resulting single-level optimization problem. In this paper, we investigate whether, for broad classes of MIBLPs, the resulting standard bounds admit uniform improvements that can be computed within the same computational complexity regime. For pure continuous bilevel linear programs, we show that, unless [MATH], neither the SLR-based lower bound nor its associated upper bound can be uniformly improved in polynomial time, even for the class of min-max problems. We then extend this analysis to the class of pure integer min-max bilevel linear programs under the assumption that the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse. First, we show that the continuous relaxation of the SLR admits no uniform polynomial-time computable improvement. We then prove that neither the SLR itself nor its associated upper bound admits a uniform improvement by a polynomial-time algorithm with access to a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) oracle. Importantly, this rules out uniform improvements by iterative MILP-based approaches, including cutting-plane-based and decomposition algorithms. Overall, our results demonstrate that the SLR-based bounds are, in a complexity-theoretic sense, unimprovable systematically within their natural computational regimes.
tldr: This paper analyzes whether standard single-level relaxation bounds for mixed-integer bilevel linear programs can be uniformly improved in polynomial time, proving complexity-theoretic unimprovability under standard assumptions.
motivation: Exact MIBLP algorithms rely on lower and upper bounds initialized from the single-level relaxation, and it is unclear whether these standard bounds admit systematic polynomial-time improvements.
method: The authors use complexity-theoretic reductions and hardness arguments—conditioned on P≠NP and the non-collapse of the polynomial hierarchy—to show that no polynomial-time algorithm (even with MILP oracle access) can uniformly improve the SLR-based bounds.
result: For continuous bilevel linear programs, neither the SLR lower bound nor its upper bound can be uniformly improved in polynomial time unless P=NP, even for min-max problems; the same holds for pure integer min-max bilevel LPs and for MILP-oracle-based iterative approaches.
conclusion: The standard SLR-based bounds are essentially unimprovable within their natural computational regimes, ruling out uniform improvements via cutting-plane or decomposition-style iterative MILP methods.

title: The Role Of Concentration In Determining NaCl Nucleation Mechanism: A Story Of Pathways Coexistence
authors: Sapna Sarupria Porhouy Minh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deciphering the microscopic details of crystal nucleation remains a key open problem in chemical physics. For aqueous sodium chloride (NaCl), the extent to which nucleation involves amorphous ion aggregation, and the supersaturation regime in which two-step-like behavior emerges, remains actively debated. In this work, we examine NaCl nucleation at 12, 13, and 14 mol/kg ([MATH]) using unbiased path sampling with [MATH]RETIS. Through a combination of reaction coordinate analysis, joint and conditional probability distributions, diffusion tensor analysis, and conditional free energy landscapes, we identify nucleation pathways without a priori mechanistic assumptions. While all concentrations are governed by the same reaction coordinate, indicating that nucleus growth and structural ordering are central to crossing the barrier, the nature of reactive trajectories changes with supersaturation. At lower concentrations, nucleation mainly occurs via tightly coupled increases in cluster size and ordering, compatible with a one-step-like mechanism. As concentration increases, amorphous aggregation becomes increasingly decoupled from crystallization, and pathways involving substantial amorphous growth prior to crystallization become progressively more probable. Importantly, these pathways coexist within a single broad reaction channel rather than proceeding through distinct metastable intermediate states. Together, these results reconcile earlier, contradictory reports on NaCl nucleation mechanisms and support a view of nucleation as an ensemble of competing reactive pathways whose relative probabilities vary continuously with supersaturation. More broadly, our findings illustrate that substantial mechanistic diversity can emerge within a classical nucleation framework, without requiring distinct non-classical descriptions.
tldr: Unbiased path-sampling simulations of NaCl nucleation at high concentrations reveal coexisting one-step-like and two-step-like pathways within a single broad reaction channel.
motivation: The microscopic mechanism of NaCl crystal nucleation, particularly whether it proceeds via amorphous ion aggregation and in which supersaturation regime two-step behavior emerges, remains debated.
method: The authors use unbiased path sampling ([MATH]RETIS) at 12, 13, and 14 mol/kg together with reaction coordinate analysis, joint/conditional probability distributions, diffusion tensor analysis, and conditional free energy landscapes.
result: All concentrations share the same reaction coordinate, but as concentration increases amorphous aggregation decouples from crystallization and pathways with substantial amorphous growth become more probable, coexisting within one broad channel rather than distinct metastable intermediates.
conclusion: The findings reconcile contradictory reports by viewing nucleation as an ensemble of competing reactive pathways whose probabilities vary continuously with supersaturation, showing mechanistic diversity can arise within a classical nucleation framework.

title: Global Optimization Framework For Automated Low-Thrust Gravity-Assist Trajectory Design
authors: Ryo Iijima, Kenshiro Oguri, Toshinori Kuwahara
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravity-assist trajectory design requires searching numerous leg combinations, but applying nonlinear programming (NLP) for low-thrust trajectory optimization to all combinations is computationally prohibitive. Therefore, conventional frameworks first perform broad search using lightweight trajectory models such as Lambert-based calculation and simplified deep-space maneuver models, while pruning infeasible candidates. However, to maintain efficiency, conventional approaches handle only low-dimensional formulations with limited constraints such as up to a couple of impulse maneuvers per leg. Consequently, they cannot accommodate the constrained multivariable optimization required for low-thrust design, running the risk of prematurely pruning viable trajectories. To address this, this paper introduces a convex pruning approach capable of solving constrained multivariable problems directly within broad search while retaining the computational efficiency. We then augment the broad search stage with a robust local low-thrust optimization algorithm based on thrust regularization, which together enable global exploration and optimization in an automated fashion. We apply the proposed framework in a BepiColombo-inspired scenario involving nine gravity assists, successfully demonstrating its broad search capability to discover a far greater number of solutions (36,335) compared to a conventional approach (4,664) while identifying a wider feasible launch window by one year.
tldr: The paper presents a global optimization framework for automated low-thrust gravity-assist trajectory design, combining convex pruning with thrust-regularized local low-thrust optimization.
motivation: Gravity-assist trajectory design requires searching enormous numbers of leg combinations, and applying nonlinear programming to every combination is computationally prohibitive, so existing broad-search frameworks use only low-dimensional models and risk prematurely pruning viable low-thrust trajectories.
method: The authors introduce a convex pruning approach that solves constrained multivariable problems directly during broad search while remaining computationally efficient, and augment the search stage with a robust local low-thrust optimization algorithm based on thrust regularization.
result: In a BepiColombo-inspired scenario with nine gravity assists, the framework found 36,335 solutions versus 4,664 for a conventional approach and identified a feasible launch window extended by one year.
conclusion: The proposed framework enables automated global exploration and optimization for low-thrust gravity-assist trajectory design, substantially outperforming conventional broad-search approaches.

title: The Car Resequencing Problem With Makespan Minimization
authors: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois C\^ot\'e Xinyi Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Problem definition: The car resequencing problem involves rearranging the sequence of cars between two adjacent production shops via an intermediate buffer. This study explores a new variant that aims to minimize the resequencing makespan when the buffer features several forward lanes and a return lane (RL). Both types of lanes follow first-in-first-out rules, but operate in opposite directions. Through the RL, cars can circulate between forward lanes, thereby increasing resequencing flexibility and complexity. The goal is to position cars over time to complete the target sequence change in the shortest possible time. Methodology/results: We prove the problem is NP-complete and develop an exact two-stage branch-and-price approach integrated with constraint programming (BP-CP). Three versions of the master problem (MP) are proposed for the first stage, each paired with a subproblem defined on a specific graph. Using partial integer solutions from branching, a constraint-programming model built in the second stage yields either a feasible solution to the problem or a feasibility cut added to the MP. Experimental results indicate that BP-CP greatly increases the scale of solvable instances for a production batch, especially with a moderately relaxed MP. A comparative analysis shows that the RL markedly enhances resequencing flexibility, enabling smaller buffers to attain makespans comparable to those of larger buffers without the RL across varying resequencing complexities. Managerial implications: Expanding lane capacity alone yields limited gains in resequencing performance and may even reduce efficiency. The RL acts as several forward lanes, supporting a smaller and cost-effective buffer design while maintaining efficient just-in-time operations.
tldr: This paper studies a new variant of the car resequencing problem in which a buffer with forward lanes plus a return lane is used to minimize the makespan of reordering cars between two production shops.
motivation: Resequencing cars between adjacent production shops is a practical bottleneck in automotive manufacturing, and existing buffer designs with only forward lanes offer limited flexibility, motivating the study of a buffer augmented with a return lane.
method: The authors prove NP-completeness and develop an exact two-stage branch-and-price approach integrated with constraint programming (BP-CP), using three master-problem variants each paired with a graph-defined subproblem and feasibility cuts.
result: Computational experiments show that BP-CP substantially increases the size of solvable production batches, and that the return lane markedly improves resequencing flexibility, letting smaller buffers match makespans of larger RL-free buffers.
conclusion: Adding the return lane supports smaller, more cost-effective buffer designs, whereas simply expanding forward-lane capacity yields limited or even negative gains in resequencing performance.

title: Decentralized Network Congestion Control For DAG-based Distributed Ledger System
authors: Mayank Pandey, Rachit Agarwal, Sandeep Kumar Shukla, Nishchal Kumar Verma
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a variable and behavior-based node-specific proof-of-work (PoW) model for a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based distributed ledger technology (DLT) network to mitigate decentralized network congestion control. Network congestion control for centralized communication systems is an established field of study, with detailed and continuous research being done on the subject. However, attention to congestion control in decentralized networks is relatively recent and underexplored, especially with DLT, such as blockchain and DAG-based networks. For the DLT networks, the network congestion is caused by factors such as transaction spamming, an increase in the user base, and the launch of new tokens. We focus on the congestion caused by the spamming of transactions within the blockchain and DAG-based DLT network. Based on the network throughput of transactions per second and consensus procedure, the DAG-based DLT needs to control network spamming more than the blockchain network. The PoW model within the DLT consensus framework is a limited deterrent against spamming. Our model provides equal opportunities for all stakeholders regardless of their computational resources. It prevents and penalizes any node that attempts to spam or dominate the network with more than the prescribed number of transactions. Since the system nodes compete to issue transactions with finite network resources, we display the system behavior through a non-cooperative game. Further, we show that our model enforces prescribed behavior amongst the nodes through the proof of the existence of Nash equilibrium in the game.
tldr: The paper proposes a variable, behavior-based node-specific proof-of-work model for DAG-based distributed ledger networks to control transaction-spamming congestion, analyzed as a non-cooperative game with a Nash equilibrium existence proof.
motivation: Congestion control in decentralized networks, especially DAG-based distributed ledgers, is understudied compared to centralized systems, and existing PoW is a weak deterrent against transaction spamming and resource-dominant nodes.
method: A node-specific PoW scheme assigns variable difficulty based on node behavior, and the interaction among competing nodes is modeled as a non-cooperative game whose Nash equilibrium is proven to exist.
result: The model equalizes opportunity across stakeholders regardless of computational resources and penalizes nodes that spam or dominate the network beyond the prescribed transaction count.
conclusion: Behavior-based PoW can enforce prescribed node behavior and mitigate congestion in DAG-based DLT networks, as supported by the game-theoretic equilibrium analysis.

title: Generalizations Of Two Ramanujan Series For $1/\pi$
authors: Kunle Adegoke
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By utilizing two known hypergeometric summation identities we extend two well-known Ramanujan series for [MATH] by making each of them a member of an infinite family of series. We also find the corresponding families involving harmonic numbers and odd harmonic numbers.
tldr: This paper generalizes two of Ramanujan's classical series for 1/π into infinite families using known hypergeometric summation identities, including variants involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.
motivation: Ramanujan's series for 1/π are celebrated for their rapid convergence and deep connections to modular forms and hypergeometric functions; extending them into parametric families is a natural pursuit in classical number theory.
method: The author applies two known hypergeometric summation identities to deform the original Ramanujan identities, generating infinite parameterized families of 1/π series and analogous families with harmonic and odd harmonic number coefficients.
result: Each of the two original Ramanujan series is shown to be a special member of an infinite family of series for 1/π, and corresponding harmonic-number families are derived.
conclusion: The work broadens the known landscape of Ramanujan-type 1/π identities, though it remains a purely analytic number-theoretic contribution with no apparent overlap with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: On One-sided Series Of Bessel Functions Of The First Kind: $\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} (\pm 1)^m J_{Nm+p}(x)$
authors: Matwey V. Kornilov
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present generic expressions for one-sided series of Bessel functions of the first kind: [MATH] and [MATH]. The result is expressed in terms of incomplete Lipschitz-Hankel integrals of Bessel functions of the first kind, which can be represented as Kamp\'e de F\'eriet functions.
tldr: The paper derives generic closed-form expressions for one-sided series of Bessel functions of the first kind, expressed via incomplete Lipschitz-Hankel integrals and Kampé de Fériet functions.
motivation: One-sided series of Bessel functions appear in various applied and pure mathematical contexts, but generic closed-form evaluations were lacking; the author aims to provide such expressions.
method: Analytical derivation manipulating infinite series of Bessel functions J_{Nm+p}(x) with alternating signs, reducing them to incomplete Lipschitz-Hankel integrals and representing those as Kampé de Fériet hypergeometric functions.
result: Generic expressions are obtained for the series sum_{m} (±1)^m J_{Nm+p}(x) in terms of incomplete Lipschitz-Hankel integrals, which are further expressed as Kampé de Fériet functions.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of closed-form evaluations for Bessel function series, potentially useful in mathematical physics and special-function theory, but it has no direct bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Powell-Style Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization With Complexity Guarantees
authors: Abraar Chaudhry, Katya Scheinberg, Scholar Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.09441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose variants of model-based trust region derivative-free algorithms that are closest to methods initially proposed and implemented by Powell.
